He walks best using a headcollar harness and a dual-control lead, as he can be strong on the lead but is improving with training. Felix could potentially live with a calm, well-mannered female dog, but he may react if approached aggressively by other dogs.

Due to the lack of background information and his size and energy levels, Felix would be best suited to an adult-only home or one with children aged 12 and over. He is not cat tested, so his compatibility with cats is unknown.

An experienced owner who has previously had large-breed dogs is recommended to help guide Felix into a balanced adult life.

name: Artie
description:
Artie is a gentle, one-year-old Shepherd mix from Cyprus who is ready to start a new life after being found abandoned in a municipal pound.

Artie is a true sweetheart who is looking for the opportunity begin again. He’s a young dog, estimated to be no more than one year old, and he has already experienced more hardship than any dog should.

He was found abandoned in a municipal pound before being taken in by one of our shelter partners when space became available. Understandably, he arrived frightened and unsure, with signs that he had not received the kindness or care every dog deserves.

Despite his difficult start, Artie has shown himself to be a calm, gentle and sensitive boy. He is not naturally trusting of new people and tends to hang back when meeting someone for the first time, but his shy nature is never defensive. Instead, he quietly observes, waiting until he feels ready to approach.

He will come to you ever so gently and slowly when he’s ready, you just have to earn it! With time and understanding, he begins to show interest, especially if you happen to have a biscuit in hand. Treats have become an important part of his confidence building journey and are really helping him learn that people can be kind.

Among other dogs, we have noticed that Artie has a naturally soothing presence and has formed some lovely bonds with other dogs in the shelter, particularly those who are nervous or have similar temperaments.

He has been a quiet source of comfort to many of them, offering calm companionship and helping them to feel at ease. For this reason, we believe Artie would thrive in a home with another friendly, well-adjusted dog to show him the ropes and offer reassurance.

He is still learning to trust the world around him and will need an adopter who understands the importance of moving at his pace. Artie would do best in a peaceful, semi rural home with access to a secure garden and without too much hustle and bustle.

A household with older children, ideally aged ten and above, would suit him better at this stage, as younger children may feel overwhelming for him. He has not yet been tested with cats so we have no insight as to how he may react to a resident feline.

Artie is a work in progress, but what he lacks in confidence he makes up for in heart. He is a gentle boy with no malice in him, only the quiet hope that life might finally offer him the love and safety he has missed out on so far.

With time, consistency and lots of patience, we believe Artie will come into his own and become a truly devoted companion.

If you are looking to make a real difference to a dog’s life and believe in the quiet power of kindness and patience, Artie may just be the one.

name: Indiana Jones
description:
Indiana Jones is a 1-2 year old male Cross-Breed, currently at our holding kennels in Southern Spain. He was thrown over the fence at the municipal pound one night and left to his fate.

Unsurprisingly, when admitted into our care, he was very nervous, and he is still a bit wary of people that he doesn’t know. However, the moment he realises that you are not going to hurt him, he’ll jump up and shower you with kisses!

Indi is a medium active dog and loves to run but in moderation. He is also good with all the other dogs at the shelter and loves to play with them.

Indi would be better in a home with another resident dog as he gains confidence from having other dogs around. He will need a low-activity quiet home who can give him lots of time.

Indiana Jones is negative for all infectious diseases, including Brucella canis.

name: Benji
description:
BENJI is a 4 year old male podenco, currently at our holding kennels in Cordoba, Southern Spain.

We rescued Benji from a very busy municipal pound in central Spain. He had been collected by the authorities from a breeding hunter with his two equally terrified siblings, and was having a terrible time, sitting and shaking at the back of the pen, only daring to venture out if food was thrown.

He is much more confident since arriving at the shelter but it’s still difficult for him to trust – he still finds it difficult if somebody makes a quick movement or if he hears a loud noise, which is completely understandable given his background.

An escape artist, he jumps and scales very well so his adopter will need to be experienced with this type of dog and put into place proper security measures to keep him safe.

He loves other dogs and finds security in having them nearby so a home with a resident dog or dogs is essential for Benji. Ideally, a home in Spain is sought so that Benji doesn’t have to travel, but we will consider the UK if the right home is found.

Benji is a Podenco and was a working dog – please research the breed-specific needs of the Podenco before applying.

All of our dogs have an international passport (unless born in the UK) and are microchipped. They are fully vaccinated for standard diseases as well as rabies and kennel cough.

All dogs are blood tested for infectious diseases including Leishmaniasis, Dirofilaria, Ehrlichia, Babesia, Anaplasma, Lyme and Brucella canis.

All dogs, unless there are medical or behavioural reasons to not do so, will be sterilised. Benji is neutered. Please note that we will advise medical results and treatments upon successful application.

Adoption contract and fee, homecheck, adoption checks and lifetime RBU (rescue back-up) apply as standard.

name: Taffy
description:
Taffy is a one year old German Shepherd cross and was brought into the shelter by the dog wandering after she was found wandering through the fields as a stray.

She wasn’t difficult to catch as she was more than happy to see new humans and trot over to them! She’s now very patiently waiting for her second chance, hoping that her new family are out there.

Taffy is estimated to be around a year old and as appears to be a theme with our shepherd girls, she’s so clever. The boys aren’t quite at their level just yet!

Taffy is very smart and similarly to Birdie, who came in a few weeks before her, she also new some basic commands which suggests she’s had a home, or at least positive human interaction (maybe from a farm owner or outside an army base) from someone.

Taffy now shares her kennels with another dog and although she was initially a bit disgruntled about having to share her space with a male dog, they’ve since really started to get along.

She will grumble at him a bit if he’s invading her space or jumping on her too much, but between them they seem to have sussed out their new friendship and are getting on just fine.

Taffy could definitely live alongside a resident dog in her new home, but she’s a confident girl and doesn’t seek out their company.

Being a shepherd, Taffy is not only smart but she’s also fiercely loyal and very active. She would thrive in a home where she has access to a secure garden to run around in and sunbathe, and she would also be best suited to a family who enjoy an energetic lifestyle.

Getting the opportunity to explore would be perfect for Taffy, and she’ll be a great partner in crime on an adventure or a long hike.

She is still getting used to lead training, but thanks to the volunteer visits at the weekend she’s getting more familiar and confident. She loves being outside, watching the birds, rolling about in the grass and sniffing about in the dirt.

But, when she’s had her fun outdoors she is more than happy to chill out in her kennel, and she loves inching herself closer and closer to you until she’s finally resting in your lap. She has the mindset of a small dog and is definitely not aware of her size!

Taffy is a really good girl and we would love to see her shine in a new home where she has the focus, commitment and love she’s due. She is a wonderful character and will only continue to blossom.

name: Astra
description:
Astra is a 2-year-old female Croatian Shepherd Cross.

Astra is suitable for living with children over 8 years old and can get along well with other dogs, making her a great addition to families with older children and existing dogs.

However, she has not been tested with cats, so her compatibility with them is unknown. Astra is a loyal, easily trained, and loving dog.

Although she is not completely house-trained since she currently lives outside with her siblings, she is expected to learn quickly.

Astra is castrated, vaccinated, and microchipped.

Her adoption fee is £475, which includes a home check and full rescue backup provided by Ninas Haven, ensuring comprehensive support for her new family.

name: Jako
description:
Jako is a 2-year-old male Croatian Shepherd Cross.

Jako is suitable for living with children over 8 years old and can get along well with other dogs, making him an excellent fit for families with older children and canine companions.

However, he has not been tested with cats, so his compatibility with them is unknown. Jako is a loyal, easily trained, and loving dog.

Although he is not completely house-trained since he currently lives outside with his siblings, he is expected to learn quickly.

Jako is castrated, vaccinated, and microchipped.

His adoption fee is £475, which includes a home check and full rescue backup provided by Ninas Haven, ensuring comprehensive support for his new family.

name: Brock
description:
Drop dead gorgeous Brock is a two year old Pointer/Bully mix and arrived at the shelter a couple of months ago after the dog warden brought him in as a stray.

We were assuming someone would come and collect him, as he was in great health and was so happy around people, but sadly days turned into weeks and no one came to get him.

Brock is now searching for a new home where he can be treated like the prince he truly is!

Brock is estimated to be around two years old and definitely has some kind of hound in him among various other breeds – he’s a real mixed bag but so handsome.

He has stunning markings which look very Bracque, and he is also very people oriented and clever. He is keen to please and loves to impress people. He learned a gorgeous sit in just a few tries and now sits beautifully waiting for a treat in his kennel.

Brock would be best suited to a home where he’s the centre of attention. Since being in the shelter he has been fine with female dogs, but he is more picky with male dogs and doesn’t really like to share his space with them.

With this in mind he would also be better suited to a family that have experience of owning dogs before, just so they feel comfortable managing interactions. With people though, Brock is an absolute superstar and just adores everyone.

Brock would be happy in a home with a fairly active lifestyle and someone who wants to work a bit more on his training. As he’s clever, he really enjoys learning and benefits from some focus and direction.

He also has potential to enjoy scent training, as he loves to use his nose like – typical hound! He would also prefer a home with access to a nice garden.

Brock would be great with children and he loves any kind of attention. He can be bouncy and excitable, so with that in mind children aged 8+ are probably more appropriate.

Brock would make an amazing adventure companion and would love to opportunity to spend lots of time outdoors. He has plenty of stamina, and would relish the opportunity to become the apple of someone’s eye.

He is very loyal and loving, and as long as someone is comfortable with him not being the best of friends with every single dog he meets, he could absolutely shine in the right forever home.

name: Chicago
description:
Hi, I’m Chicago — a 3 year old male Jura Hound Cross.

I might not be the kind of dog who runs straight up for cuddles, but I’ve come such a long way, and I’m really proud of how far I’ve come.

Not so long ago, I was abandoned in a killing pound, completely petrified and shut down. It was clear I had never truly known kindness or felt safe around people. I was so scared that I couldn’t even imagine what love or trust could feel like.

Then CYDRA came into my life and rescued me. Slowly, I started to discover that not all humans are bad. Step by step, I’m learning that life can be good.

These days, I’m brave enough to sit quietly while someone puts my lead on, and I even get excited when I know it’s time to go outside — that’s where I feel my happiest. I love running around doing my zoomies, feeling free, and I’ll even come over for treats now.

When I first arrived, though, things were really tough. I was suffering from a severe ear infection that caused me constant pain. Despite months of treatments and efforts by the vets, it just wouldn’t get better.

Eventually, the only option left to give me the pain-free life I deserved was surgery to remove my ear canal. It was a big decision, but it changed my life for the better.

Since the operation, I’ve transformed into a much happier and more confident boy. I’m so much more at ease and genuinely enjoy being outdoors, exploring, and even being around people.

Right now, I’m still on my journey to trust fully. I know there’s a social, playful boy inside me, just waiting for the right family to help him shine. I’ll need time, patience, and lots of understanding, but I promise I’m worth it.

I’m looking for a quiet, countryside home where I can continue to grow at my own pace. I would love to have another calm, confident dog by my side to show me the ropes and help me build even more trust.

If there are children in my future home, they should be over 12 and comfortable giving me the space I sometimes need.

I was bitten by a sandfly and developed leishmania, but don’t worry — it’s dormant and under control thanks to treatment. I just need to take an inexpensive daily medication and have regular blood tests (twice a year) to ensure it stays that way.

My rescuers are very knowledgeable about leishmania and assure me that it’s manageable and won’t shorten my life if monitored properly. Plus, it’s not contagious to humans or other animals.

If you have a big heart, a peaceful home, and the patience to help a boy like me learn what true love and happiness are, I promise I’ll do my very best to become the loyal, joyful companion you’ve been dreaming of.

Could you be the family who helps me find my confidence, my joy, and my forever place in the world?

name: Aspen
description:
Meet Aspen, a 2 year old female Labrador Retriever — the regal Lab girl with a free-spirited heart.

The regal Lab girl with a free-spirited heart. When we first saw her, we couldn’t believe it.Who could abandon a Labrador like Aspen? A dog with no flaw, no “issue,” no reason — only grace, loyalty, and joy.

She stood there in that cold prison kennel… smiling. As if to say: “This is not the end for me.”Aspen is everything a dog parent could dream of:

Positive, stable, affectionate, radiant. She runs with the wind, plays with dogs, rests gently under your legs, and greets each day with that signature Lab smile.

Her name suits her perfectly: Aspen — strong and beautiful like the tree, rooted in nature yet free in spirit. She is a reminder of everything we love about Labradors: their sunshine, their loyalty, their endless capacity for joy.

Aspen is ready — not just to be adopted, but to be cherished.To be that dog who runs by your side, rests at your feet, and fills your life with the love only a Lab can give.

Will you give this elegant black Lab her forever story? Please get in touch to find out how to adopt her today!

name: Noah
description:
Noah is a two year old cross breed and is every bit the silly goofball that he looks to be in his photos. We love this daft boy, and he came to us a few weeks ago after being found as yet another wandering stray.

Unfortunately for Noah, in terms of appearance he is the kind of dog that we often see overlooked for a long time – we don’t know why, they just always seem to take longer!

We’re hoping that just maybe he’ll get lucky before he has to spend months on end behind bars.

Noah is around two years old and full of fun. He is such a positive dog and despite his life in the shelter being relatively boring, any moment of excitement that he does get to experience, he does so with 100% enthusiasm.

He loves any kind of human interaction and is beside himself with happiness when someone goes into his kennel to spend time with him. He’s a very sociable, human focused dog and just wants to be loved.

Noah shares his kennel with a quiet, older female dog, and despite his energy he understands that he needs to give her some space and calm down when she’s not feeling it.

He seems to be able to read canine body language well, and we think he could live with or without other dogs.

He appreciates their company and seems to enjoy an opportunity to play when it’s offered, but he is also very people oriented so doesn’t depend on other dogs to feel secure and confident.

Noah is young and still very bouncy at times, although a lot of this is due to lack of exercise and no outlets for his excitement.

With a proper routine and lots of lovely long walks, we’re sure he will calm down, but it would still be in his best interest to have some entry level training, to learn the basics and improve his manners.

He is so keen to please and very food motivated, so he loves to learn! He has already perfected a very nice ‘sit’ in the shelter, and looks extremely proud of himself whilst doing so.

Noah has a huge heart and so much love to give. He’s looking for an active home with a garden, someone up for the fun that a younger, more energetic dog can bring into their household, and someone that can also shower him in the love that he craves.

He will make the absolute best friend once he’s had a chance to settle in and find his feet.

name: Prince
description:
Prince Charming is a 3-year-old male Akita. He is currently looking for a new family to love and care for him after arriving at the shelter in November 2024 as a stray. It is puzzling why no one came forward to claim him, as he is a lovely boy with an engaging personality.

Once he settles into his stride, he walks well on the lead, showing that he can be a reliable walking companion. He enjoys the company of other Akitas and appears to be comfortable walking alongside them.

However, Prince can become a bit excitable when he sees smaller dogs during walks, so it is recommended that he be placed in a home with a large breed, spayed female dog, following successful introductions.

His food motivation is a significant advantage in ongoing training, as it helps him learn new commands and behaviours. He already knows how to sit and give a double paw but has plenty of room for improvement and learning.

At the kennels, Prince enjoys running around and is quite energetic, relishing the chance to jog alongside his human companions. He would thrive in an active household where he can partake in daily exercise and enjoy games of chase.

His playful nature is evident when he showcases his Akita zoomies, and he loves to play fetch, although he may not always return the toy.

As Prince is a stray, the shelter is keen to find him a suitable home, ideally without children or with older children aged 12 years and above. This ensures a peaceful environment for Prince, where he can continue to adapt and thrive in his new family.

name: Raya
description:
Raya is a one-year-old female cross-breed dog, currently residing in a private shelter in Romania.

She exudes a particularly calm, quiet, and obedient nature, longing for a loving home to call her own. Despite her young age, Raya displays remarkable maturity and doesn’t engage in conflicts with her fellow shelter dogs.

She has been spayed, vaccinated, microchipped, and undergone thorough blood testing, ensuring her good health and readiness for adoption.

Raya craves companionship and is seeking a household with someone who can dedicate plenty of time and attention to her.

She is proficient in walking on a lead, showcasing her adaptability and readiness for urban life.

Consider welcoming Raya into your home; she promises to be a delightful companion with her gentle disposition and loving nature. For an adoption fee of £425, you can provide Raya with the forever home she deserves.

A home check is requested to ensure the suitability of the environment for Raya’s well-being, and rescue backup is available for ongoing support.

Raya can be delivered to your doorstep, facilitating the adoption process for potential owners. Don’t miss the opportunity to make Raya a cherished member of your family.

name: Cassie
description:
Cassie is a one year old Shepherd mix and was found running through farmland when a local rescuer was able to coax her into her car and take her to safety.

Surprisingly, during her check up at the vets they discovered that she actually had a registered microchip, so they were able to track down her owners and asked them to come and collect her.

But of course, had the story ended positively, then Cassie wouldn’t be on our website. Sadly, her family said they didn’t want her anymore as she was too energetic, and that the rescuer could rehome her.

There was no sense of remorse or accountability, they just gave her away and moved on with their lives.

Cassie is a shepherd mix and she is indeed an energetic, active and highly intelligent young dog. She’s estimated to be just under a year old, and she is always raring to get outside and go on an adventure.

Right now, she’s in private kennels where she’s safe and sound until she finds her forever home, but she needs more exercise and enrichment than they can offer her, and as a result whenever she goes out for a run in the yard she is like a coiled spring.

Cassie is looking for a family who have had high energy dogs before and can give her the physical and mental outlets that she needs to thrive. She is so, so loyal and bonds with people very quickly.

She’s extremely keen to please and eager to learn, and as she’s so food motivated this makes the perfect reward!

Cassie would be best suited to a home outside of the city with an active family who enjoy running, exploring and just generally being outdoors.

When her needs are met, like any dog, Cassie is a bundle of love and loves hanging out with people. She’s also great with other dogs, especially those of a similar energy level to her, and she loves racing around in the grass with them.

She would also be best suited to a home with a reasonable size garden, as she really likes being outdoors.

Cassie may be young and bouncy, but she also has lots of love to give. She is the perfect dog for someone seeking a best friend, adventure partner and a companion that they can train.

name: Jess
description:
Jess is a 7-year-old female Cross-Breed. She is a medium-sized dog weighing 16.6kg and measuring 20cm in height.

With some Shepherd-type traits, Jess has a distinctive appearance and a strong personality to match.

Jess has had a difficult time building confidence, and her anxiety can sometimes lead to behaviours that appear aggressive toward unfamiliar people.

This behaviour stems from fear rather than aggression, and with the right support, she has shown encouraging progress.

She has nipped a few people in the past, but she now wears a muzzle without issue during her walks.

Training has helped her make great strides, and once she builds trust, Jess becomes a deeply affectionate and loving companion.

Jess is searching for a very specific home—rural, quiet, and with plenty of space where she can roam freely without the stress of unfamiliar people.

It’s a rare kind of home, but one she truly deserves.

name: Buddy
description:
Buddy is a 3 year old male Dachshund cross Collie. He lives in Royston, Hertfordshire, where he is patiently waiting for his forever family to find him.

Buddy is a charmingly odd-looking pup. He’s lively and playful, he enjoys spending time outdoors and loves his daily walks. Buddy does walk very well on a lead but still prefers a collar to a harness.

Buddy is extremely affectionate and attached to the people he trusts; once a person wins his heart, he will be their most loyal, loving friend forever.

Buddy’s full of unconditional love and always ready for a good, long cuddle. At the moment, Buddy is struggling with self-confidence. He is making good progress and already learned to tolerate scary noises like thunder, TV or loud machinery and hardly flinches nowadays.

Buddy is, however, still intimidated by strangers, especially when he’s concerned they are invading his territory. He wants to keep his family safe and whenever strangers approach, he can get vocal to warn them.

Buddy is much more relaxed around women, and given time, he warms to most people. He is often timid around new dogs too and does not like cats.

Buddy is a really sweet, loving boy and we would love to find a family ready to give him all the time and consistent training he needs.

We’re sure he is capable of overcoming his struggles and becoming a more confident pup. Buddy is not neutered yet, as consultations with two vets suggested that it could worsen his fear.

name: Cece
description:
Cece is an 18 month old Shepherd mix who arrived at the shelter as an unclaimed stray, a story we’ve heard many a time. No one came looking for her, and she had no microchip or collar, so who knows where she came from.

She was however in good health, and happy to meet new people, so we’re hopeful that she’s not had a difficult start in life.

Cece is around a year and a half old and she is a beautiful girl with a very happy, friendly and sociable personality. She loves being around people and is very eager to please, quietly confident, and reads other dogs well.

It took a little while for her to initially calm down when she first arrived in the shelter as she had some nervous energy to burn off, but once we’d found her the ideal kennel mates and she’d had some time to decompress, her true nature started to shine through.

As mentioned, Cece now shares her kennel with multiple other dogs of various sizes, ages and energy levels. She’s loving having the opportunity to make new friends and enjoys playing with them and just being in their company.

While we don’t feel she’s dependant on other dogs, she definitely likes hanging out with them, and she’s more than happy to share her bed, which is so cute.

18 months old is still young, so Cece would benefit from some basic training to help refine her manners a little. She learnt to sit in no time, despite all the distractions around her in the shelter.

As she is food motivated, this works really well as a reward. When she’s excited to see you Cece is prone to jumping up a bit, but it doesn’t take long for this to pass and with some routine and a proper home setting, we’re confident that is very trainable.

The ideal home for Cece would be with a family who enjoy time outdoors, have direct access to a secure garden, and who are keen to invest some time into a young dog learning about a whole new world.

We think the outskirts of the city would be preferable for Cece, or of course a more rural setting would suit her just fine too.

She’d enjoy a fairly active lifestyle, and with some time and patience we think she will make a brilliant addition to a family home.

name: Ernesto
description:
Ernesto is a beautiful boy 4 years old 25 to 30 kg a Collie cross very friendly with people. He was a few months in a public shelter in Romania before being save to a private shelter over there.

In the public shelter as seen in one of the videos he was with other dogs but in the private shelter he is all alone in his pen (second video) because they feel he doesn’t like other dogs.

Ernesto has a very sad life he’s been 2 years now in the private shelter and never gets out.

Such a frustrating life for this young boy. Is there anyone with experience who can offer Ernesto the life he deserves a fun active life with people who have got lots of time for him as we don’t want him to be lonely any more.

Ernesto is a great boy with so much joy to give. Please change his life. No children. Not cat tested. Ernesto is vaccinated blood tested neutered and microchipped.

He is ready any time to be transported to your home. Adoption fee £450 . A home check is requested. Rescue back up.

name: Gina
description:
Gina is a four month old cross breed. Gina’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

Gina is very confident among the group and can be a bit bossy with her siblings! She is a girl who knows what she wants, and sometimes that is the limelight!

She is always very eager to say hello to passing visitors that walk by her kennel, and she loves any opportunity to be be cuddled or played with.

She also loves chasing after a toy, a pebble or a stick – it doesn’t matter what it is, she can make a game out of anything!

Gina isn’t familiar with the lead just yet, but she’s starting to learn that it’s a positive thing now. She is super excitable and bouncy when she gets the chance to interact with people, and she bonds fiercely with those that she loves.

She is definitely going to be a very loyal companion, we have no doubt about that.

Gina is good with other dogs and on the most part she gets along well with her siblings, but she needs a bit of work on sharing. She could definitely live alongside a resident dog, and an older, calmer dog would be a great influence on her.

However, we also think she is confident enough to be the only dog in the household.

The ideal home for Gina would be a loving family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city. She would prefer a home with access to a garden, and this will also help with house training.

As she grows into an adult dog, she will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and of course being a puppy she will both enjoy and benefit from some introductory training.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Gina has had some initial exposure to children and we think she would be great for a family with school age children. She can be a bit nippy in her play, but that is purely to do with her age.

She is still a puppy, so it’s important that there are boundaries in place if she’s living alongside kids, for both parties! Given the opportunity, we know Gina is going to grow up into a lovely young dog with a great personality and nothing but devotion for her new family.

name: Grant
description:
Grant is a four month old cross-breed. Grant’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

At a glance, Grant looks just as confident as his siblings. He’s always at the bars of the kennel jumping up to meet new people with his brothers and sisters, and the fact that he’s the only pup in the litter with huge ears also draws a lot of attention to him.

However, Grant is actually the most nervous of the pups. As soon as he’s separated from his siblings, he is very unsure of what to do.

He is such a sweet, soft and gentle boy, and he just needs a slightly more patient, calm and understanding home who can go at his pace. We’ve seen so many pups like Grant in our time and the power of the perfect home cannot be underestimated!

Grant is a submissive boy and he’s always a little unsure around new people until he knows that they’re going to treat him with kindness.

When he gets to know you, he likes to just sit beside you and chill, and he loves an ear scratch or a belly rub.

He’s not confident on the lead yet so that will take a bit of work, but there’s not a bad bone in his body and he really does want to trust people, he just takes a little longer than his siblings.

Grant would be better suited to a home with another resident dog that he can learn from and play with. As soon as he’s away from his siblings, he panics and is visibly less confident.

Another dog would definitely help his transition from shelter to sofa, and help him feel less overwhelmed and confused.

The ideal home for Grant would be a loving, patient family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city.

As Grant is more nervous than his siblings, a calm home in a quieter area would be great for him, and we’re sure his confidence will grow once he’s settled and feeling more secure.

As he grows into an adult dog, he will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and some basic training.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Grant is just a baby and has never had an adverse reaction to a child, but in order to keep things predictable for him we’re looking for a home with older children only.

He just needs some time and understanding to come out of his shell, and he’s only a few months old right now – he will change so much within the first few months of his adoption and it will simply take a special, caring family to give him the love and support he needs.

We’re already seeing glimpses of the silly, charming and playful little pup he is, and it will be so rewarding to see him really flourish with his new family.

name: Gilly
description:
Gilly is a four month old cross-breed. Gilly’s litter, aka the G pups, arrived at the shelter in June after they were all found living together as strays without their mum.

They were terrified to begin with and spent a lot of time huddled together in their kennel, completely overwhelmed and frightened. After a few days they gradually started to get a bit braver, and now they’re ready for adoption.

Gilly is such a cutie and has a really joyful energy about her that makes it impossible not to love her. She gets so excited to spend time with people, and she gives so many kisses!

She’s also quite happy worming her way into your lap for a little rest while she takes in everything going on around her – she just loves being involved.

Gilly is a clever girl and is quick to learn new things. She has pretty much learned to sit for a treat already, and although she’s a bit suspicious of the lead at the moment she’s started to trust that it’s not a bad thing anymore.

She has an every wagging tail and a very happy personality, and as she’s very sociable we’re sure it won’t take long for her to make plenty of new friends!

Gilly is great with other dogs and would be more than happy living alongside a resident dog that she can learn from and play with.

She’s a very friendly girl and reads other dogs very well, but we also feel that she would be confident enough to be the only dog at home.

The ideal home for Gily would be a loving family home that are looking for a young dog to raise outside of the city. She would prefer a home with access to a garden, and this will also help with house training.

As she grows into an adult dog, she will be looking for a moderately active lifestyle, and as she clearly loves to learn she’d also benefit from (and enjoy!) some basic training.

At just four months old the G pups are still very much learning each and every day. There are lots of different personalities within their litter, but they’re all growing and changing at their own pace.

Each of them will need patient, understanding families who recognise that adapting to a companion lifestyle will be a very new concept for all of them, as they’ve never lived in a home before.

And as with any puppies, they will need continued socialisation, training, and plenty of company.

Gilly has had some initial exposure to children and we think she would be absolutely great living alongside kids. She is still a puppy, so it’s important that there are boundaries in place if she’s living alongside kids, for both parties!

But as she is so affectionate and playful we think she would love having little people to befriend. She’s a super little character and we know she’s going to make someone very happy!

name: Fred
description:
Fred is a 9 year old male Golden Retriever Cross.

Our poor golden retriever beauty, Fred, was surrendered to the shelter days before his ninth birthday, after spending his entire life being owned.

Unfortunately, his family wouldn’t let him live indoors and refused to make the necessary arrangements to accommodate him living outdoors (which is legal in Cyprus), and veterinary services ended up getting involved.

Fred was extremely stressed when he was brought into the shelter and we’ve spent the last few weeks getting to know him and realising how much he’s actually missed out on over the years.

He may have had a family, but he has had minimal socialisation, very little training, no one to rely on and a lot of instability. In fact, three years ago we actually found Fred miles away from home.

He’d been living on a picnic site for weeks before he was reunited with his family via his microchip.

So now, in his senior years, Fred needs an entirely new beginning. He is looking for a patient, understanding and confident family who recognise that he needs time to adapt.

Although he’s nine years old, he’s very active, strong and bouncy, especially when he gets overexcited. He is therefore not suitable for a home with young children as he has no concept of his size and strength.

Being part retriever, Fred is absolutely obsessed with food. He knows how to sit, and he also offers a very gentle and polite paw, but he inhales his food and any kind of treat is welcome!

He also loves water and loves splashing around in the paddling pool on a hot day. And despite his older age, he’s really still a puppy at heart.

He loves his toys, especially a teddy that he can rip apart as he loves taking the stuffing out of things. He also enjoys playing tug with a rope toy, and chasing after a ball (although he’s not sure on the concept of fetch).

Fred hasn’t been very well socialised with other dogs and this is an area that needs some continued work. He is generally good with females, but the first time we introduced him to other dogs we could see in his body language that he just had no idea what to do.

He’s had very limited interactions with other dogs sadly, so he’s not ready to just go into any home and mingle with lots of resident dogs.

Fred does bond quickly with people though and responds really well to kindness. He is a silly, goofy boy with a huge heart and ultimately all he wants is to be adored. He loves a belly rub, he loves playing, and he is sociable and friendly.

He is looking for a family who recognise that he’s been let down over the years and needs a little more guidance, patient and understanding. There is SO much love in this dog, and in the right home he will absolutely blossom.

name: Prince
description:
Prince is a 20 month old Lurcher and he is looking for a new home. Although he’s not originally an Underdog, when we heard that he needed some support we wanted to try and help him.

Unfortunately, Prince is living in a home that is not suitable for his needs. He has been struggling in the city and needs a less overwhelming environment to call home.

He is also a very energetic boy, and is looking for an active, patient and understanding family.

Prince is just under two years old and is a sighthound mix. He was part of an accidental litter, and was bought as a puppy, but has consistently struggled in London and requires a more experienced handler.

With the support of a local day-care and dog walking business, Prince has had a lot more exposure to other dogs and new people, and he has made a lot of progress regarding his confidence and social skills.

We think this will continue to improve in a semi-rural area.

Prince is adorable and has a very loving, affectionate nature with those he knows. He loves to give cuddles and is really friendly once he has formed a bond with you.

He is however apprehensive of strangers, and needs time to get used to new people. Although Prince doesn’t like being in big groups of dogs in day-care setting, he is very happy on group walks and trots along happily with them.

Prince has been handled quite roughly in the past which has left him sensitive to touch. He has been muzzle trained to make vet visits more manageable, and he also wears this when on walks in case he meets a dog he feels uncomfortable around.

During the day, Prince is quite happy to be left alone for a few hours. He is housetrained and enjoys playing with toys. He has been conditioned to race after a ball when out on walks, so this is his primary source of exercise and he is very ball driven.

He has responded well to training and is generally a very good boy who is eager to please. He sits and waits for his food and takes treats nicely, but doesn’t like to be approached whilst he is eating.

Prince loves spending time in the countryside where he has more space to run around. He would love a home with a big garden and an active lifestyle, and he’s much calmer outside of the hustle and bustle of London.

We would love to see him get the second chance that he deserves in a more suitable home where he can get the attention, focus and training that he thrives on.

name: Aspen
description:
Aspen is a 10 month old Beagle mix who’s life got off to a very rocky start. He was abandoned as a young puppy in Cyprus and found seriously unwell with parvovirus.

After spending time in the vets and making a full recovery, he joined the shelter and eventually travelled to the UK as a foster.

Since arriving, it’s been a bit of a journey for him, and it’s taken time to really understand what he needs to feel settled and secure.

After struggling to find the right fit in a home environment, Aspen has spent the last couple of months in kennels, where he has surprised everyone with just how well he’s done.

With clear routines, patient handling and consistent care, he has really come into himself. He’s responded brilliantly to basic training, built very strong relationships with the staff and grown hugely in confidence.

Aspen is a clever, energetic young dog, but new and unfamiliar situations can still feel overwhelming for him, and are often made more challenging by the fact that he is deaf.

Aspen is great with people and has been incredibly sociable, affectionate and engaged with those caring for him. Everyone who has been involved with him at the kennels has been really charmed by his personality.

He’s a cheeky, busy puppy who loves cuddles, fuss and being the centre of attention. Once he feels safe, his personality really shines and he shows just how much he enjoys human company.

When it comes to other dogs, Aspen is more selective. While he has previously lived alongside other dogs, is kennelled parallel to other dogs, and can pass dogs calmly on walks, we think that overall he would be happiest as the only dog in the home.

We suspect that earlier experiences may have left him feeling automatically defensive, and giving him a space where he doesn’t have to share attention or resources will help him relax and feel secure.

We are looking for an adult only home without other pets. As Aspen is deaf, it’s important that his environment is predictable and calm, and we don’t feel it would be fair to place him in a home with children or cats.

He would thrive in a quieter, more rural setting with access to a garden and plenty of opportunity to burn off energy in a safe way.

Aspen is clever and has learned hand signals for certain commands, so he would love to continue with further training as he really likes to learn and engage.

Aspen needs a confident, committed adopter who understands that he’s a young dog who has had a lot of upheaval in a short space of time.

With the right people, he lights up and shows what a sweet, silly and loving boy he really is.

Experience with training or deaf dogs would be helpful but isn’t essential, as long as his new family are patient, open to learning and ready to give him the structure and stability he’s been missing.

name: Otto
description:
Otto is a handsome seven year old Beagle who originally came from Cyprus and was adopted amid the pandemic. He spent a while in foster with our Head of Adoptions, Eve, before travelling to the UK to meet his new family.

Sadly, he is now seeking a new home due to the arrival of a new baby, which has disrupted the calm environment he was used to.

Otto is an affectionate, cheeky and characterful boy who has been a much loved member of his family for several years. He absolutely loves people and is happiest when he’s receiving plenty of fuss.

He enjoys curling up on the sofa for cuddles, sneaking onto a comfortable bed and finding the warmest spot in the house for an afternoon nap.

He’s a particular fan of sunshine, radiators and heated floors – you can take the dog out of Cyprus and all that! He hates the cold and the rain, and will always sidestep a puddle, and he’s also not a fan of loud noises, motorbikes, or fireworks.

He’s a funny little character with plenty of personality and a love of relaxation and home comforts.

When he’s not enjoying a cosy afternoon indoors, Otto loves getting out and exploring. He’s an adventurous boy who enjoys long walks, trips to cafés and pubs, car journeys and even lengthy hikes.

As a typical Beagle, his nose is often glued to the ground and he loves investigating interesting scents. He walks well on the lead, but his recall is less reliable in open countryside.

Otto is generally very sociable with people and other dogs. He enjoys meeting his canine friends in the park and has happily spent holidays alongside other family dogs.

He could potentially live with another calm, compatible dog, although he can occasionally be uncomfortable around larger entire males.

He’s also comfortable with visitors, even if he likes to announce their arrival with a bark! Otto knows his basic commands, is housetrained and is very responsive to training, especially when tasty treats are involved.

One area where Otto needs understanding and guidance is his tendency to become possessive over toys. He enjoys collecting things and can become defensive if someone tries to take them away.

His family have found that exchanging items for treats works well, but this is something his new adopters will need to manage carefully.

Otto would love a home with people who enjoy being outdoors but are equally happy to spend a relaxed afternoon together.

He has lots of affection to give and would thrive with an adopter who can offer him companionship, enjoyable walks and consistent boundaries around his toys.

His family adore him and have not made the decision to rehome him lightly, but they know that a quieter home without young children will allow him to feel more comfortable.

We know just how much Otto has so much to offer as a funny, affectionate and adventurous companion, and he will happily fill his days with sniffing, exploring and finding the perfect place to curl up beside his favourite people.

name: Murphy
description:
Meet MURPHY, a gentle, loving, and resilient small boy around 4.5 years old, who resembles a charming mix of Corgi and Chihuahua. He is a Ukraine war dog in need of a safe haven.

Available for a foster-to-adopt. Already in UK: Clapham (London), SW11. Adoption fee reduced.

He lost one eye in a horrific incident in Ukraine, but his spirit remains unbroken. He’s now in the UK and looking for a forever home where he can be cherished. Sadly, the family who took him in feels they are not the right match for him and are unable to meet his needs.

They have provided a thorough evaluation of MURPHY, which you can read below.

Rescue Story:MURPHY’s story is one of love, resilience, and heartbreak. He was abandoned in a communal garden in Ukraine, where he was embraced by the local residents. They cared for him, and he became part of their extended family, playing with children and happily resting in his little kennel.

Tragically, some cruel teenagers thought it would be amusing to chase MURPHY and throw a petard into his kennel. After the explosion, MURPHY was left severely injured, his face burned and bleeding, and his eye tragically lost. However, despite this horror, MURPHY’s spirit remained unbroken.

He was rushed to a clinic, treated, and later brought into a rescue. Through it all, MURPHY continued to trust humans, showing the true resilience of a dog’s heart.

A Word from His Current Family:“ He is a lovely little dog, with a strong and great spirit. Murphy is a rescue from Ukraine who came to us in June 2024. He only has one eye due to an incident where he was attacked by some teenagers who threw a firework / explosive into his little den.

Since then he was taken into care and fostered for.

A highly independent little soul, he loves his alone time and is never anxious in these periods. He loves his sleep and will find sun spots and cozy little nooks to snuggle up in.

Positives? Good to be left alone for short periods, very calm and sleeps a lot? Doesn’t destroy things in house? Independent? Enjoys good play time and belly rubs when he rolls over? Not a fussy eater? Will sit for snacks and treats? Handsome? Very low maintenance, will shed a couple times a year.? Travels well, loves car and train journeys

Needs? Child free house? A quieter house, less footfall to not disturb him? Only dog in house

Things to know? Give him space and wait for him to come to you. He will and he loves chin and ear scratches? Resource guard, work on splitting his meals up and make him back away from food bowl before topping up. He has improved.? Don’t pick him up? Leave alone when in his bed (trained safe space)? Keep on lead when on walks? Takes pain relief pills for previous accident.– has snapped on occasion, when was misunderstood, but not regularly and not his fault. Needs patience and understanding for all he’s been through

Due to his injuries and impaired vision he can be easily startled if approached from his right.

Requiring a very calm and peaceful life. Super low maintenance and highly independent, he is equally happy when alone or in company of owners. Give him space and wait for him to come to you, he loves chin and ear scratches. He’s a great little dog to have around and keep you company.

He will nuzzle up to you for some love and scratches and then spend the rest of night tucked up in his bed. He has adapted well to his new life in the UK and is very healthy.

Fully vaccinated and blood tests all came back healthy. He doesn’t require long walks and can be tired out after half hour to an hour”

MURPHY is fully healthy (but missing one eye), neutered. All core vaccines are complete, microchipped, and C.Brucella tested (owners will receive a licensed laboratory test certificate).

name: Iris
description:
Iris is a 2-3 year old female Lurcher. She is great with people. Iris will need a pet and child-free home.

We are looking for either a foster or a forever home. She’s a fun-loving dog. Who just wants to be loved? If you think you can offer her lots of love and a sofa to sleep on.

name: Millie
description:
Millie is a beautiful temperament, always happy, loving cross-breed girl of around 2 years old.

She is super friendly with everyone – kids, dogs, cats. Great on the lead. Housetrained. Based in Peterborough, available for foster-to-adopt. Reduced adoption fees

Unfortunately, a few days ago, Millie had to go to boarding kennels as all our current fosters are fully booked. While this is likely one of the best kennels you can find, staffed by true dog lovers with great facilities, an on-site behaviorist, and a focus on rehabilitation, it’s still not the same as a home.

They offer wonderful care, take the dogs on walks, and play with them, but it can’t replace the love and comfort of a real family. We’re praying that this sweet girl finds her forever home soon.

Before this Millie was at foster in UK and this is what they say:

“Millie is a very sweet, attractive and affectionate young dog. She likes people and to be with people and is normally docile and friendly. She likes to be stroked and groomed and to have her belly rubbed.

She likes exploring but doesn’t try and escape from the garden or run off when out for a walk. She likes to play with toys, especially in the evening out in the garden. She will readily sit on command and shake a paw!

She is very good off the lead, walking along paths, in fields and in the woods etc in the countryside, and she will regularly look back and check that you are there and come back when called.

She is very friendly with people she meets and will regularly sniff them (to check they are human) as you walk along, though she is slightly nervous of other larger dogs until she gets to know them. She will happily chase and play with other dogs she feels comfortable with. If they are too much she will do a little growl and they will usually back off.

However, we have come across a few behavioural issues. The main issue appears ‘resource guarding’ and the things she guards have increased and changed whilst she has been with us. This can be unpredictable and takes us by surprise at times. For instance we might be happily working in the same room as Millie who’s in her bed, coming and going and talking to her.

Suddenly she will change and growl, snarl if we re-enter the room. She also will suddenly and unpredictably snarl in other places where she’s lying down. Another example is that we are both hesitant of trying to move her off the sofa.

The only safe way is to call her from another room, sometimes with a treat to lure her. This may be because for some reason Millie has not really settled with us after nearly four weeks and still feels insecure.

I think Millie will need to be with family who are experienced with dogs, who can interpret her body language and behaviour, and be able train with her to reduce and prevent her very marked resource guarding (rescue will be happy to provide useful and working materials to treat it). I think this shouldn’t be a family with young children but teenagers and older children should be okay if they are aware of what not to do.”

MILLIE is active but not hyper, always happy, not pushy. Very loving and loves cuddles and fuss. Loves people company and being nearby.

MILLIE is very smart, loves learning new things. But the most she likes is walks being active and having attention from people.MILLIE is good in the car and loves it.

MILLIE has no known health issues. Spayed, vaccinated, microchipped. Brucella C. tested.

name: Ava
description:
Ava is a 6-year-old female Cross-Breed who is very friendly and playful.

She has been neutered, microchipped, and vaccinated, making her fully prepared for her new home.

Ava weighs approximately 28 kg and stands around 48 cm tall.

This sweet girl is eager to find a home where she can be loved and cared for.

Ava’s playful nature and friendly disposition make her a delightful companion.

She would thrive in a home where she can receive plenty of attention and affection.

name: Bailey
description:
He is a super boy and a lovely goofball. Bailey is neutered, vaccinated, and microchipped, making him ready for his forever home.

Standing at approximately 60cm tall and weighing around 40 kg, he is a friendly and sizeable companion.

Despite his large stature, Bailey’s gentle nature makes him an ideal addition to any loving household.

He is eager to find a home where he can share his affection and playful energy.

Bailey’s charming personality makes him a delightful companion for anyone seeking a loyal canine friend.

name: Pennie
description:
Pennie is an 13 months old, female, cross-breed pup who, along with her siblings, faced abandonment in woodland in Romania at a very young age.

Fortunately, they found refuge in a foster shelter where they have been nurtured ever since.

This sweet and slightly shy pup exhibits a calm demeanor, making her an ideal companion for those with experience in dog ownership.

As a good-sized medium dog, Pennie will undergo neutering before embarking on her journey to a new home in the UK.

Her health is meticulously documented in her pet passport, with full vaccination and microchipping completed.

Comprehensive blood tests have been conducted to ensure a smooth integration into her new life.

Pennie, being fully cat-tested with a video available for potential adopters, proves her compatibility with feline friends.

Ideally suited for a family with older children due to her size, Pennie would thrive in an environment where her adopters possess previous dog ownership experience.

To facilitate a seamless transition, we offer full rescue backup and a commitment to ongoing support, ensuring the continued well-being of our canine charges.

Pennie eagerly awaits a loving home, ready to bring joy and companionship to a family in the UK.

name: Holly
description:
Holly, 1 year old female Cross-Breed, and her two sisters were found dumped by waste bins in an alley in Romania at six weeks old.

They have been in a foster shelter since then, and their English foster mum has brought them on well.

They are in a pen with some other pups and a surrogate mum and dad dog, which teaches them doggy manners!

Holly is neutered and fully vaccinated. She is also microchipped.

She would be delivered directly to her new owners once admin checks have been done.

It would be wonderful if she could have a doggy friend to live with, but this is not essential.

Two of her kennel mates have already travelled to their new homes in the UK, and it would be lovely if Holly could too.

Full rescue backup is given on all of our dogs.

name: Freya
description:
Freya, a 5 year old female Labrador Cross, has been patiently waiting in the foster shelter for quite a while after being rescued from a kill shelter in Romania.

We can’t understand why someone hasn’t fallen for her before.

Freya loves attention from her humans and lives with other dogs.

She has been neutered and fully vaccinated as well as microchipped.

She would be delivered directly to her new adopter once admin checks have been carried out.

Please consider this lovely girl for a place on the Happy Bus to a new life here in the UK.

name: Inky
description:
Inky, also known as Blinky, is a very cute whippety lurcher boy of around 2 years old, looking for a special forever home.

He is a loving, affectionate boy who thrives on companionship and enjoys being part of the family. When he arrived in foster care, almost 8 months ago, he was in a very poor physical condition due to previous neglect.

He had flat feet caused by a lack of proper nutrition and calcium, as well as severe corns on his feet and infected toes which made walking very painful for him.

The corns later required surgery. He underwent three weeks of daily bandage changes and treatment, which he handled incredibly well.

His feet have improved significantly, but adopters should be aware that corns can recur in some dogs and may require monitoring and future veterinary care.

EGLR are happy to contribute towards this. Inky is great on the lead and enjoys his walks, he can become very boisterous and can be a little reactive at first when seeing other dogs and very jumpy when meeting new people but this is just excitement.

His recall is very good in a secure environment. His absolute favourite game is fetch, and he can happily spend time chasing and retrieving his toys.

He also loves trips to a secure field where he can stretch his legs and enjoy himself. Around the home, Inky is a real cuddle bug.

He loves nothing more than snuggling up on the sofa with his people and will happily curl up beside you for an evening of relaxation.

He sleeps well through the night, although if given the opportunity, he may quietly sneak onto the bed and burrow under the duvet, especially when it’s cold! very whippety behaviour. He is fully house trained and not destructive.

Inky travels brilliantly in the car and settles quickly, making him an excellent companion for adventures. He can be left for up to four hours with another dog.

He may bark initially when left but soon settles down. He generally gets on well with other dogs, although he can be a little dominant around some male dogs.

Because of this, he would be best suited to living with a female dog. Due to some issues around female handlers, Inky is looking for an adult-only home with male owners.

He won’t cope living with children and needs a home where there are no visiting children. Inky has worked with professional trainers and has made great progress.

His foster carers have learned techniques that help him succeed, and support can continue for adopters based in the Worcestershire and Gloucestershire areas. Inky is a wonderful, loyal dog with so much love to give.

In the right environment, with understanding, dog experienced owners who can continue the guidance he’s already received, he will make a devoted and affectionate companion.

This dear boy has been through so much in his short life and experienced so much pain, inky really deserves the best home we can get him.

name: Liquorice
description:
Liquorice, 15 month old male Lurcher, is quite honestly one of the sweetest, silliest and most lovable boys you could ever wish to meet. He is an incredibly sociable lad who absolutely adores people.

I genuinely haven’t met a person he doesn’t greet like a long-lost friend!

Even when he was having to attend the vets twice a day to have his wound cleaned, he would arrive with his happy, waggy tail, seemingly forgetting all about the discomfort of his visits and simply looking for love, attention and cuddles.

One of the lovely things about him is how adaptable he is.

He has enjoyed lots of house visits, happily meeting and greeting new people, and has even had a couple of overnight stays at different foster homes, settling in straight away as though he’d lived there forever.

He’s also had the opportunity to meet lots of different dogs during these visits, and making new friends is definitely one of his favourite things to do!

Liquorice is continuing to build up his confidence with being left alone and is now managing a couple of hours after having been walked and fed.

This is something his new family will need to continue working on gradually. He’s an excellent traveller in the car and really is a pleasure to take out and about.

On walks, Liquorice can be a little strong on the lead. Some of this is down to him adapting to his new walking gait as a three-legged boy, and some is simply his excitement at being out exploring the world!

He’s getting fitter and stronger every day and is already enjoying around 30 minutes in the morning and 40 minutes in the evening.

At weekends, we sometimes swap this for one longer walk. He’s still a young boy with plenty of energy, and as his fitness continues to improve, he’ll need a family happy to provide him with the exercise and adventures he enjoys.

And finally, we must mention Liquorice’s other great passion in life… TOYS! Liquorice is a master toy destroyer. If there’s stuffing inside, he will find it!

His new home will need to provide him with a plentiful supply of toys for him to lovingly de-stuff, as this is quite possibly his favourite pastime. So, what sort of home is Liquorice looking for?

We think this lovely boy would be happiest in a home: Without cats. With another friendly dog to play with and share adventures.

With children aged 12 and over. With a secure garden where he can enjoy some playtime and burn off some of that cheeky energy.

Liquorice has been through so much, yet he continues to greet every day and everyone he meets with the happiest of hearts. He doesn’t let having three legs stop him enjoying life, and he has so much love to give.

We’re looking for a family who will embrace his cheeky personality, enjoy his enthusiasm for life, continue supporting his progress and, most importantly, love him unconditionally.

Could you be the one to give this very special boy the forever home he’s been waiting for? We think you’re going to fall head over heels for him.

name: Jam
description:
Jam is a female mixed breed puppy aged around 5 months. As a guess she will be medium sized when fully grown. Jam fostered in Norwich, Norfolk.

Jam has grown up at the public shelter in Botosani. We met her on our most recent visit and she is one of the lucky pups to come on transport to England.

Due to being a young puppy, we are looking for a forever family where there is an adult at home for most of the day. All puppy adopters will need to work on training throughout their young life and anticipate accidents.

Isn’t yet cat tested but young enough to be trained to be appropriate around a cat.

name: Walter
description:
Our extra special boy Walter is approximately eight years old and a rather large hound of sorts. Walter weighs twenty-seven kilos and measures fourteen inches from shoulder to paw.

Very sadly Walter has spent half of his life in our Cyprus shelter having been surrendered by his owner.

Walter is the absolute favourite of the shelter staff and volunteers. His attractiveness is instigated by his wisdom, prudence and calm demeanour.

Walter has a near mystic charm which wins hearts and minds rapidly. Such a stunning boy with a huge presence.

Absolutely a handsome chap with a wonderful coat and ears that are totally extraordinary. Really Walter could hardly be more deserving and will make a fabulous new family member for a very fortunate adopting family.

Walter exudes charm and elegance on his lead and enjoys his time in the car. He seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs, cats and children.

name: Jello
description:
Jello is a female mixed breed puppy aged around 5 months. As a guess she will be medium sized when fully grown. Jello fostered in Norwich, Norfolk.

Jello has grown up at the public shelter in Botosani. We met her on our most recent visit and she is one of the lucky pups to come on transport to England.

Due to being a young puppy, we are looking for a forever family where there is an adult at home for most of the day. All puppy adopters will need to work on training throughout their young life and anticipate accidents.

Isn’t yet cat tested but young enough to be trained to be appropriate around a cat.

name: Reyna
description:
Reyna is an eight year old female Border Collie. Reyna is in a wonderful foster home in Cambridgeshire.

She shares her foster home with several resident dogs and although we think she’s lived a sheltered life without much interaction, with their guidance, she’s really learned how to interact and enjoy the company of other dogs.

Although very nervous when she first arrived, she has slowly but surely come out of her shell with the guidance of her foster family and has even been for some little adventures to a cafe!

She can still be shy of new people but she’s affectionate with everyone, especially her foster mum who’s a firm favourite since she does all the walks!

Her character is coming out as she gains confidence and she can be a lovable cheeky monkey! She’s a real joy to watch as she grows and learns that the world can be a fun and safe place to be.

She travels well in the car, eager to jump in for a walk! She’s also picked up house training very well too. Her foster mum calls her the perfect dog.

She gets on well with all the resident dogs but the other resident collie is a firm favourite! She is looking for a home with a kind and patient family who can carry on all the amazing work of her foster home

Reyna is a Border Collie. Her Spanish passport says she is eight years old but the vet thinks she might be younger.

Reyna was given to the shelter in Spain along with her three puppies (Ares, Sena and Zeus) by a family who kept her outside her whole life. We think she had been chained up for most of that time and hadn’t had the chance to interact with humans much or other dogs.

Reyna’s Spanish passport says she’s almost 8 years old but the vet thinks she might be younger.

If you are interested in giving wonderful Reyna a home, she is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Reyna is currently in Cambridgeshire but she is ready to travel to her forever home. Will that be with you?

name: Mandy
description:
Mandy is a 5-year-old female Cross-Breed. She’s a calm, gentle soul who has already been spayed and fully vaccinated, weighing around 23 kilograms.

Mandy is currently safe in a private shelter in Romania after being rescued from a kill shelter earlier this year — and now she’s patiently waiting for her forever home.

This lovely girl has a relaxed, easy-going personality. She loves simple pleasures like pottering around a garden and finding a comfy spot to nap in.

Mandy doesn’t need a high-energy household; she’s happiest in a calm environment where she can enjoy her surroundings and be close to her people.

She gets along beautifully with other dogs and has no trouble sharing her space with feline friends either. Mandy’s sociable yet serene nature makes her a wonderful companion for homes with other pets.

She could also live with dog-savvy children aged 10 and above, as long as they understand her gentle and steady temperament.

Although Mandy enjoys the company of other dogs, she doesn’t necessarily need one in her home. She’s quite content being the only dog as long as she receives love, care, and companionship from her humans. What she does need, however, is a secure garden — a place to wander, relax, and soak up the sunshine.

Mandy represents everything lovely about a rescue dog: calm, affectionate, and grateful for every bit of kindness shown to her.

Her adopters will also receive full rescue backup and support throughout the adoption process and for the lifetime of the dog, ensuring Mandy’s smooth transition into her new life.

Home checks and an adoption donation apply, as the rescue ensures every placement is the perfect fit. Whoever opens their home to Mandy will be rewarded with a loyal, gentle friend who embodies peace and love in every wag of her tail.

name: Duke
description:
Duke is a six year old male Pointer. Duke is a very handsome boy!

Duke was handed in to the shelter we work with in North Spain by a hunter as he was no longer wanted. He has a slender and elegant figure, he is of medium size and a balanced character and is respectful of the other dogs at the kennels.

Duke currently shares his kennel with a female Setter. He shares the space without problems including at dinner time.

Duke is a little shy if he doesn’t know you, but he quickly gains confidence and approaches timidly seeking cuddles and caresses.

His recall is good within the confines of the shelter but it would be a different matter on an exciting walk. He loves to run around the enclosure and stretch his long legs.

If you are interested in giving wonderful Duke a home, he is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Duke is currently in Spain but he is ready to travel to his forever home in the UK.

name: Kylo
description:
Kylo is a 4 year old, medium sized, lab-cross and is literally the friendliest boy. He simply adores being around humans and will be the best companion.

Oh and he knows some tricks! When he arrived at the shelter he was microchipped so he had some sort of home at some point in his life.

He craves love and attention from everyone he meets, even if just meeting for the first time. He’s very smart and will be a joy to train.

Kylo is a very sweet boy and has a puppy-like energy where he is just happy and excited to be with you and show off his tricks. And he’s very food oriented!

Some dogs in the shelter he accepts, others he doesn’t. Although this can be a product of the stress of shelter life, it’s best if he is an only dog.

Kylo can be quite energetic and will likely need an active home. He would even make a good running buddy. He already walks well on the leash.

Kylo can be adopted in the UK or Cyprus. His adoption fees are sponsored so, if travelling to the UK, we are just asking for travel costs to be covered.

He is ready to fly. He is vaccinated, castrated, and has had a full health check and blood tests for infectious diseases.

Full rescue back-up is provided by Saving Souls Animal Rescue, a UK-based registered charity.

Foster placement, foster view to adopt, and adoption all considered.

name: Angel
description:
I’d like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need a kind doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need an extra secure garden, at least 6ft+ where I will be safe!

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

22-11-26 Angel is an inquisitive but timid lady who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is desperate to be brave and, although she is still a little unsure of us, she showed us that there is a lovely, curious girl hiding beneath those nerves. She is now happy to approach us and although does get a little shy she seems to enjoy some gentle tickles. Her tail was even wagging for her photos, which was lovely to see! We think that with a little time and reassurance, Angel will soon begin to blossom and show us more of her personality.

Angel would be best suited to a calm home with adopters who have experience of worried ex-breeding dogs and who have plenty of time to spend with her as she settles in to her new life. We would consider homing her with dog savvy children 9+. She will need an extra secure garden of at least 6ft to keep her safe as she has been known to climb.

Angel gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Angel has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, walking on a lead and harness and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient and understanding, allowing her to take things at her own pace as she gets used to her new surroundings.

Angel has already shown us that she wants to be brave, and we think it will be a wonderful thing to watch her confidence grow. With love, patience and a friendly canine companion by her side, she has every chance of becoming a happy and cherished little member of the family.

Angel has been given the Gift of Life by Brenda Gray

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Afon
description:
I’d like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to exercise in with 6ft+ fences.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have a lump on my neck, which will be assessed.

21-11-26 Afon is a shy little guy who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start.

Despite his quiet nature, he has been showing us just how brave he can be. Afon will come over to say hello, offer us little kisses on our hands and happily accept a gentle fuss. He seems eager to make friends with us, and it is lovely to see him finding the courage to approach and enjoy some attention. We think there is a sweet, affectionate little chap hiding beneath those initial nerves.

Afon gets on wonderfully with his kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so he will need a kind resident dog in his new home to help guide him and give him the reassurance he needs as he settles in and finds his paws.

He would be best suited to a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and will allow him to settle in at his own pace. We would consider homing him with dog savvy older children aged 9+.

As Afon has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. His new family will need to be patient and understanding, giving him time to adjust and learn at his own pace.

Afon has already shown us that he wants to make friends and enjoy human affection. With a loving home, a little patience and a friendly canine companion by his side, we hope he will continue to grow in confidence and become a very special little companion.

Afon has arrived with a grape size lump on his neck which will be assessed by our vets.

He has a travel document which says he is a poodle cross but according to his microchip he is a Goldendoodle x Miniature Poodle.

Afon has been given the Gift of Life by Sarah Conner
