name: Milo
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I will need to be the only dog in my new home, so all of the attention is on me!

I will need an extra secure garden, at least 6ft+ where I will be safe!

I walk well on a lead but will need my adopters to be understanding of my needs!

I have lived in a home before so may I may already know the basics.

I will be neutered before finding my forever home!

06-10-26 Milo is a super sweet boy who has come to us from a home through no fault of his own. Sadly, he has already been through more changes than a young dog should have to, and he is understandably a little worried in new environments. He takes a lot of comfort from people he knows, but once he feels comfortable, his fun and affectionate personality really starts to shine.

Milo is an incredibly sweet boy who absolutely loves being close to his people and thinks he is the perfect lap dog! He is happiest when he can have a cuddle and will happily climb up for a lap sit. He is a sensitive little soul and will need a kind and patient home where he can continue to build his confidence and learn that he is safe and secure.

Milo will be looking for a home where he can be the only dog and get all the fuss and attention for himself. We are told that he has had a previous incident with a cat and so he cannot be homed with cats or small furries and must be kept on lead unless in a secure area.

Milo has missed out on some socialisation, but he is currently working on his social skills and is making lovely progress. He can happily walk alongside calm dogs and has had some nice greetings. He doesn't always know what to make of other dogs yet and can sometimes get a little carried away when mixing, but with continued positive socialisation we are sure his confidence will grow. He can also react if another dog barks at him first while on lead, so his new family will need to understand this and help him learn how to navigate these situations.

Milo will need an adult-only home with people who have experience of bull breeds and understand what sensitive souls they can be.Although he is a wonderful boy, he would not be suitable for a first time dog owner.He will need a kind and patient family who can give him time to settle and continue building his confidence. He will also need the time he is left home alone built up gradually as he settles into his new home.

Milo will need an extra secure garden of at least 6ft to keep him safe, as he is a young and active boy who could be an escape artist if given the opportunity.

Milo is such a lovely young boy who has already been through so much change. With the right family, patience and continued socialisation, we know he will make a wonderful companion and be the loving, fun little lap dog he is so desperate to be.

name: Benji
description:
I will need an adult-only home that understands me.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I'd like a secure garden to have fun playtimes in.

I walk on a lead and would enjoy a nice walk once a day.

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

03-11-26 Benji is a beautiful, playful boy who originally came into our care as an unclaimed dog in 2024. He was adopted but has sadly returned to us because of illness in the family, meaning his owners were no longer able to care for him.

Benji is feeling a little out of sorts being back in kennels but is coping well. He is a super-loving boy who absolutely adores attention, cuddles and bum scratches. He has been spending lots of time in the office with us while his exercise is restricted and is always happy to soak up some fuss. He has lots of character and a wonderfully silly personality, and we know he would love nothing more than to be back in a home where he can relax on the sofa and enjoy life with his favourite people!

Benji can be a little reactive towards other dogs when out on walks, but having spent time in a home, he has made some lovely improvements. He is currently kennelled with a friend and we feel he could potentially live with another suitable dog or as an only dog. His adopters will need to be understanding of his needs and willing to continue supporting him with his training around other dogs. When Benji was initially with us, he could snap at feet when leaving his kennel, but this behaviour has improved massively since his time in a home. He is generally much better around doorways, although he can still become uncomfortable if someone lingers in a doorway or enters without greeting him, so his adopters will need to be mindful of this.

Having lived in a home before, Benji is familiar with the sights and sounds of everyday life and will hopefully settle back into a home routine with a little time. He needs a calm, adult-only home with adopters who understand his breed.

Benji was castrated and had nasal wedge surgery in 2024. He can still experience episodes of being sick, particularly following exercise, excitement or periods of stress. He is currently being trialled on a course of medication to see whether this helps manage his symptoms, but he may require further investigation and potentially additional surgery to address his breathing, such as BOAS surgery, in the future. His exercise and activity levels are currently being managed, so he will need adopters who are happy to accommodate his reduced exercise needs and understand that he may require further veterinary treatment and monitoring as needed.

Benji really is a lovely little man who is full of character and has so much love to give. He is a typical silly Frenchie who is desperate to get back to being the couch potato he deserves to be! With a calm home, understanding adopters and plenty of cuddles, we know he will be so happy to have a sofa to call his own again.

name: Sixpence
description:
I will need an adult only home, that will let me settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I can be a little nervous, and will need a secure garden to learn about the outdoors.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Sixpence is a nervous girl who has come to us from a breeder. She isn’t brave enough to approach you just yet, but she is easy to handle once she is in your arms. We have now learnt that she is trying so hard to be brave and, although she is still quite nervous, we are seeing little bits of her cheeky Daxi personality coming through every day.

Sixpence seems to have had very little positive touch or affection before coming to us. She has recently moved in to foster and is happy to take treats from her foster parents but is not quite sure about being stroked yet. She will allow them to put her harness on as long as she is in a quiet corner and things are taken slowly. You can tell she isn't entirely comfortable, but she trusts us enough to allow it and is always very happy to enjoy a little cheese reward afterwards! With continued positive reinforcement, we are confident that this will improve as Sixpence learns that good things can come from new experiences.

Sixpencerelies heavily on other dogs and really enjoys being around her resident dog friends. She watches what they do and follows their lead for confidence, and she has even learnt from them how to use the dog steps to get onto the sofa and watch the world go by from the front window! She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can lean on as she continues to find her confidence and learn about home life.

Penny is also discovering all sorts of things that she enjoys. She loves sunbathing, having the freedom to explore a secure dog field, stuffed teddies and, of course, cheese! She has a crate set up with a fluffy bed where she can go when she wants some quiet time to herself, and she seems to really enjoy having this safe space available to her.

Sixpence will need a calm and quiet home with adopters who have breed experience and understand that she will need plenty of time, patience and encouragement as she settles in. Her ideal home would have one or more small, friendly dog companions who can help her feel secure. We feel that children would be too overwhelming for Penny, so she will need an adult-only home.

Penny has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she continues to learn about home life, including house training. She will also need to continue her harness and lead training at her own pace, as these are still very new experiences for her.

Sixpence is a very sweet little girl who is trying her very best to be brave. She has already made some lovely progress in the short time she has been with us, and we can't wait to see just how much more of her personality comes out as her confidence grows. She just needs someone willing to give her the time, space and love she needs to discover how wonderful her new life can be.

Penny's ideal home would be a quiet one with one or more small dog friends and owners that are willing to give this girl the time and space she needs to learn her new life at her own pace. Sadly we think she would find children too overwhelming. We can't wait to see her confidence grow in her new life.

Sixpence is a nervous girl who has come to us from a breeder. She isn’t brave enough to approach you just yet, but she is easy to handle once she is in your arms. She will need time, patience and plenty of trust-building before she feels confident enough to come out of her shell.

Sixpence relies heavily on other dogs and will follow their lead, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can lean on as she learns about home life and finds her paws. She will need a calm and quiet home, with adopters who have breed experience and can understand her needs.

Sixpence has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns about house training. She is working with her kennel mummy on harness training and would like to continue this in her new home. She can live with sensible, dog-savvy teens aged 13+ who will give her the time and space she needs. Sixpence is a very sweet girl who just needs someone willing to give her the chance to blossom.

I would love one or two slow walks a day!

07-11-26 Bilbo is a gorgeous boy who has found his way into our care after spending nine years in a home before sadly being returned to his breeder. He is an absolutely lovely boy who is very much a family dog and is ready to find somewhere to enjoy his golden years.

Bilbo will be looking for a loving home with adopters who have experience with dogs of a similar breed. At the moment, we feel he would be best suited to an adult-only home where he can have the time, patience and understanding he needs to settle into his new home. Bilbo does show signs of separation anxiety and can become quite unsettled when people leave his kennel and will bark at them to try and stop them leaving. He will need adopters who are happy to work with him on this, helping him to feel more comfortable and gradually building up the time he can be left alone. With patience, consistency and lots of reassurance, we hope he will soon learn that he is safe and doesn't need to worry when his people leave him.

Although Bilbo is an older boy, you wouldn't know his age when you meet him! Bilbo is outgoing, friendly and just wants to be everyone's best friend. He walks well on a lead, although he can be a little strong at times. Bilbo is confident enough that he could be homed as an only dog as long as his adopters were around most of the time and had plenty of time to spend with him. At the moment he is kenneled alone, but we will start introducing him to other dogs and in the right circumstances he may be able to be homed with another kind female resident dog, but wouldn't like to share his home with a male dog.

Having previously lived in a home, Bilbo may already know some of the basics, although he might need a few gentle reminders as he adjusts to his new surroundings. He has some stiffness in his legs, which is to be expected with age, and he will be started on YuMOVE to help support his joints.

Bilbo has already given nine years of his life to a home, and he deserves nothing more than to spend his golden years surrounded by love, comfort and all the fuss he could ever want. We really hope someone will see what a special boy he is and offer him the forever home he so deserves.

name: Bramble
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens who respect my space.

I would like to be the only dog in my new home and cannot live with cats.

I would love a garden to run and play in!

I walk well on a lead and I would love to go on plenty of adventures!

I have lived in a home before so I may already know the basics.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

05-11-26 Bramble is a very sweet lady who originally came to us from a breeder and was adopted for a short period but sadly returned due to her reactivity with other dogs. She absolutely adores people, but she can find seeing other dogs out on walks quite overwhelming, and her reactivity stems from fear rather than anything else.

She is currently working really hard on building positive associations with other dogs and is making some lovely progress. We have found several calm dogs she is happy to walk alongside, which is a fantastic step forward! Bramble is also being muzzle trained so her future adopters can continue this training and help her feel safe when out and about, particularly in busier areas.

Bramble is looking to be the only dog in her new home, where she can have all the attention to herself without the worry of sharing her space. She can live with older, sensible and dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who understand her needs. She will need an extra-secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft, as well as adopters with previous experience of reactive dogs, her breed and ex-breeding dogs.

Bramble really is a lovely girl who is trying so hard to overcome her worries, and she has so much potential. She will need a family who understands that progress takes time, is happy to continue her training and can give her the patience and reassurance she deserves. We know that with the right people beside her, this special lady has so much to offer!

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Patoots
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

19-11-26 Patoots is a very sweet but nervous lady who has come to us from a breeder. She sat beautifully for her photo shoot and was easy to handle once she was in your arms. However, she is still shy in her kennel and doesn't approach us just yet, so she will need patient adopters who can give her the time and reassurance she needs to continue building her confidence.

Patoots takes comfort from her kennel friends and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to for reassurance as she settles in and learns about home life. She has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be understanding as she learns all about house training and walking on a lead. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens, aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in at her own pace.

Patoots is a very sweet lady who has so much potential. She just needs someone willing to take a chance on her and show her how wonderful life in a loving home can be.

Patoots has come to us hind leg atrophy which may improve with exercise in her new home. She has also had a dental where she has had multiple teeth extracted.

Patoots has been given the Gift of Life by Trudie Williams

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

23-11-26 Glenys is a nervous lady who has come to us from a breeder and is still unsure of us and being handled. However, once she starts to settle, she will allow a gentle fuss. She can be a little flighty, so her adopters will need to be mindful of this when taking her out into the garden and as she begins to learn to walk on a lead.

Glenys will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to for reassurance as she continues to build her confidence. She can live with sensible, older dog-savvy children who will understand that she needs time and patience to settle in at her own pace. Her adopters will also need to have experience with ex-breeders so they can better understand her needs.

As Glenys has never lived in a home before, her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she learns about house training and walking on a lead. Glenys is a sweet lady who is simply nervous and waiting for someone to take a chance on her and show her just how lovely home life can be.

Her travel document lists her as a Cavapoo/Cavachon, so we believe that she may be mixed with multiple breeds.

Glenys has been given the Gift of Life by Pat Smith

name: Goose
description:
I’d like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

22-11-26 Goose is a petite and gentle girl who has come into our care from a breeder in search of her forever home. She is a very sweet girl who although is quite worried and overwhelmed at the moment, will gently sniff your hands and is happy to accept a gentle fuss. We think that with love and TLC she will start to come out of her shell and will really flourish.

Goose will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and will allow her to settle in at her own pace. We would consider homing her with gentle, dog savvy children aged 9+.

Goose clearly finds comfort in the company of other dogs and loves snuggling up with her kennel buddies and will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help her to come out of her shell.

As Goose has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, walking on a lead and harness and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be very patient and understanding, allowing her to take things slowly and never expecting too much too soon.

With a calm, loving home and a reassuring doggy friend by her side, we hope she will gradually learn to trust, relax and enjoy all the little comforts of family life.

Goose has been given the Gift of Life by Bianca Romero

name: Molly
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have had 3 teeth extracted and a small cyst behind my ear drained.

08-11-26 Molly is a worried girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is a little overwhelmed to find herself here at the moment and is worried about being handled and clearly hasn't had much socialisation in her past. Despite her worries, she is a very sweet soul and with love and TLC she will start to come out of her shell.

Molly would be best suited to a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with worried ex-breeding dogs and will allow her to settle in at her own pace. We would consider homing her with dog savvy older children or teenagers who will be gentle with her.

She currently relies on her kennel friends for comfort and reassurance, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to as she settles in and continues to find her confidence. Molly has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be very patient and understanding as she gets used to all the new experiences that come with home life, including house training and walking on a lead. These things may seem quite scary to her at first, so she will need gentle encouragement and the freedom to take everything at her own pace.

Molly is a sweet girl who will need plenty of TLC, patience and reassurance to help her find her paws in this big new world. With the right home beside her, we hope she will slowly discover just how lovely life can be!

Molly has had 3 teeth extracted and has had a small cyst behind her ear drained.

Molly has been given the Gift of Life by Theresa Marshall

name: Wynter
description:
I would like an active home that will take me on plenty of adventures!

I can be an only dog or live with others, but no cats or small furries please!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I will need to learn all of the basics of the house, but I will catch on fast!

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

12-11-26 Wynter is a lovely boy who has come to us from a breeder. He is an ex-gun dog and has previously been used as a working dog, so he will be looking for an active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, adventures and activities to keep him busy. Due to his working background, he may be prone to chasing small cats and other small furries, so he will need a home without them.

Wynter is a shy boy who is still finding his confidence, but he has a lovely gentle nature and really enjoys soft toys and a bit of gentle attention once he feels comfortable. He gets along well with his kennel friends and would be more than happy to have another kind resident dog in his new home to be his friend. In the right circumstances and with adopters who are around most of the time, we would consider homing him as an only dog.

He will need patient adopters who can support him as he comes out of his shell, gets used to the routines of a home and learns about house training. He already walks well on a lead and will no doubt enjoy getting out and about once he has settled in. We would consider homing him with dog savvy children aged 9+.

Wynter is a really good boy who just needs a little time and encouragement to let his personality shine. He is ready to find a forever home where he can feel safe, enjoy an active lifestyle and start his next adventure!

Wynter has been treated for conjunctivitis, which is already much improved.

Wynter has been given the Gift of Life by Lauren Hyslop

name: Remi
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 5ft fencing.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have been spayed and am ready to find my forever home.

12-11-26 Remi is a scared little girl who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start.

She is very sensitive to touch but is trying so hard to be brave. Remi will need another kind and gentle dog in her new home, as canine companionship will be a much-needed source of comfort and reassurance for her as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Remi has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be very patient and understanding, allowing her to take things at her own pace and never pushing her into situations she is not ready for.

Remi could share a quiet home with dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to her new surroundings and a safe space of her own where she can retreat and feel secure.

Remi is very scatty when frightened, and it took three members of staff to carefully corner her for a check-up. She was so scared that she did give a little warning snap. If she feels pressured or pushed beyond what she is comfortable with, she could make poor decisions out of fear, so she will need adopters who understand the importance of careful, calm handling and allowing her choices wherever possible. She will also need a safe and secure garden with fencing of at least 5ft to help keep her safe.

Remi is a very vulnerable little girl who will need someone willing to look beyond her fears and give her the time and understanding she needs. We hope that, with a calm home, a reassuring canine friend and plenty of patience, she will gradually learn to trust and enjoy all the lovely things that life in a loving home has to offer.

Remi has been given the Gift of Life by Toni Pearse

name: Pippa
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need an extra secure garden to keep me safe.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

30-09-26 Pippa is a very scared and nervous lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is very worried about being handled and becomes stressed if we attempt to pick her up. She will try to jump from our arms and, because of this, we would consider her a flight risk and she will need fencing of at least 6ft in her new garden to keep her safe. She will need very careful handling and adopters who understand just how frightened she is at the moment.

Pippa gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Pippa has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be very patient and give her time to adjust to all the new sights, sounds and experiences that come with living in a home.

Pippa will need a quiet, confident, adult-only home where she can relax and settle into her new surroundings without too much hustle and bustle. Her adopters will need to have ex-breeding experience and understand her nervous nature and allow her to progress at her own pace.

Pippa is a very worried girl right now, but with the security of a kind canine companion and a calm, patient family, we hope she will slowly begin to feel safe and gain the confidence she needs to enjoy her new life.

Pippa has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter

name: Rizzle
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I have been spayed & am ready for my forever home!

Rizzle is a quiet and timid girl who has come to us from a breeder. When she arrived she was quite overwhelmed and in need of plenty of TLC, but she has since started to come out of her shell.

Rizzle has recently moved to a wonderful foster home where she is settling in and starting to learn about home life for the first time ever. She is making gentle progress and is even starting to wag her tail when her fosterer speaks to her and has ventured onto the sofa twice so far, although she is understandably still quite nervous and isn't yet feeling brave enough to approach but is trying her hardest to be brave.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on as she begins to gain confidence and learns that the world isn’t such a scary place.

She has never lived in a home before moving to foster, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns all about home life, including house training, though she is starting to get to grips with this already. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness as she is quite worried about being handled, but hopefully this will be introduced to her in the near future.

She is a sweet little lady with so much potential and just needs someone willing to take a chance on her. With a loving home, a confident canine companion and plenty of patience, we’re sure Rizzle will slowly find her confidence and become a wonderful companion.

Rizzle has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

Rizzle is a real sweetheart, but still very nervous, moving away from me most of the time. She has just started to wag her tail when I talk to her and has twice shared the sofa, but at a distance. If she moves into a corner, I can give her a brief stroke, otherwise she will only come for a quick sniff of my hand. She is not yet confident enough to take a treat from me. She eats well, preferring to eat alone, but not because of any guarding issues.

Rizzle has chewed toys and played with Petal, my other foster dog, but this is not a regular occurrence. She spends a lot of time alongside Petal. She is getting used to household sounds, dislikes the vacuum cleaner and goes in the garden but is OK with the washing machine, and tolerates the ironing board.

Rizzle will briefly bark if she hears a sound in the garden, eg another dog or voices. At night or if I go out, she sleeps quietly in the lounge with the other dogs. She doesn't enjoy handling at the moment, so I have not made any attempt to put a harness on her. Her toilet training is a work in progress, being clean when the back door is open.

Rizzle is a quiet and timid girl who has come to us from a breeder. She is beginning to show us just how inquisitive she can be and is trying her hardest to be brave. Rizzle isn’t quite ready to approach us just yet, but she does follow the lead of her doggy friends and takes lots of comfort from having them around. With plenty of TLC, patience and reassurance, we’re sure it shouldn’t take her too long to come around and start showing her lovely personality.

Rizzle will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on as she begins to gain confidence and learns that the world isn’t such a scary place. She has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns all about home life, including house training. She will need time to take everything at her own pace and shouldn’t be rushed before she is ready.

Rizzle can live with older, dog-savvy children who are sensible and will understand that she needs time and space to settle in. She is a sweet little lady with so much potential and just needs someone willing to take a chance on her. With a loving home, a confident canine companion and plenty of patience, we’re sure Rizzle will slowly find her confidence and become a wonderful companion.

name: Candy
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I can live with larger, playful resident dogs, or I can be the only dog in the home!

I would like a large, and secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I walk well on a lead, but I can be strong so my adopters will need to work with this

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home! Read below for more!

Candy is a very sweet and affectionate lady who has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She absolutely adores attention and cuddles and, once she gets to know you, it doesn't take her long to show just how loving she really is. Candy simply wants to be close to her people and has completely stolen the hearts of everyone she has met. She has blossomed into the most loving girl and will make a wonderful companion and is sure to become the ultimate cuddle bug in the home.

Candy has built a lovely bond with the staff member who has worked closely with her since she first arrived. She truly trusts her and has come on so much since arriving with us. Candy has such a sweet nature and it is clear how much she enjoys spending time with people she knows and trusts.

Her lead walking has improved so much too. She is now walking much better and really enjoys her outings, although her adopters will need to continue working on her lead manners so she can enjoy plenty of adventures. She has even started joining a regular volunteer on walks. Although, she doesn't completely trust him just yet, she is beginning to learn to trust him and build a relationship.

Candy mixes well with polite, well mannered dogs however she can sometimes be a little selective with choosing her friends. She doesn’t appreciate when dogs are over the top but when she does make a new friend her own play style can be quite full on! She comes away when called so we are always able to calm her down for a tasty treat. Because of her size and excitable nature, she would not be able to live with smaller breeds of dogs in the home and will need a home without cats.

As Candy is a very large lady, it is important that her adopters have experience with a similar breed and understand her needs. We have found that she can be particularly worried by formal handling, such as veterinary examinations, and finds these situations quite stressful. We will be muzzle training Candy so that she can be safely and comfortably handled for occasions such as vet visits. She recently needed to visit the vet due to sore ears and, although she found having her ears examined uncomfortable, she coped very well with the support of people she knows and trusts. She did also need to visit the vet for a check up on a day when her regular person wasn't around and found it much harder to cope with and became extremely stressed and agitated. She takes so much comfort from her known and trusted people.

Candy would be best suited to an adult-only home where her adopters can give her the time and space she needs to build trust and settle in.

Candy has arrived with a scab on the right side of her face that will be addressed during the time of her spay and is being treated for a ear infection.

Candy has come such a long way since arriving with us and is now so ready for a loving home of her own. She is an absolute angel and a true credit to her breed, with so much love and affection to give. She truly deserves someone who will give her the love, patience and happiness she deserves.

Candy will need more than one meet and greet with her prospective adopters to allow her time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Candy has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

The bond I’ve built with this lovely, sweet girl is unmatched. I feel so honoured by how much trust she has given me. She really is like my best friend, and I just love spending my days with her.

Candy is such a sweet girl, but she can be wary of strangers and a little head shy, especially when new people reach over her head to give her a fuss. Whenever we're out walking and people ask to say hello, I always explain that she's head shy and ask them to let her sniff them first and approach her at her own pace. She is more than happy to take treats from people, and it's lovely to see her little interactions.

To help build her confidence with new people, Candy now goes out with one of our regular volunteers twice a week for longer walks. She doesn't trust him 100% just yet, but she'll happily go out walking with him and take treats. She's still very aware of his presence, but it's all about time, patience and allowing her to build that trust in her own time.

Candy also had her first bath with us this week! Although she wasn't too keen to begin with, she trusted me and I made sure to respect her boundaries. We managed to wash her from the shoulders down, and I'm super proud of her! The hairdryer was a definite no, but that's absolutely fine. We do everything at Candy's pace.

She's also learnt to sit, and one of her favourite things to do is play with the squeaky balls in the yard.

Candy really does feel like my best friend at the rescue. She always makes me smile, keeps me pushing through and has such a special place in my heart. I feel so lucky to have built the bond we have, and I can't wait to see her continue to grow in confidence.

Candy is an absolute angel and a true credit to her breed. I’ve worked with her since she first arrived at the rescue, and over that time we’ve built such a lovely bond. She truly trusts me and knows that I only have her best interests at heart.

Candy has blossomed into the most loving and affectionate girl, and I genuinely love spending my days with her. She has such a sweet nature and has come on so much since arriving with us.

Candy recently had a vet visit due to having sore ears. Although you could tell she was uncomfortable while the vet was examining them, she was such a good girl throughout, and I was incredibly proud of her.

She has also mixed with quite a few dogs here at the rescue and has been brilliant with all of them. She can sometimes be a little bouncy and excitable when first meeting new dogs, but she listens when asked to calm down and is learning to manage her excitement really well.

Her lead walking has improved so much too, and she’s now walking much better and enjoying her outings.

Candy has come such a long way and is so ready for a loving home of her own. She truly deserves someone who will give her the love, patience and happiness she deserves.

Candy is a very sweet and affectionate lady who has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She absolutely adores attention and cuddles and, once she gets to know you, it doesn't take her long to show just how loving she really is. Candy simply wants to be close to her people and has completely stolen the hearts of everyone she has met. She will make a wonderful companion and is sure to become the ultimate cuddle bug in the home.

Candy can walk on a lead, although she can be quite strong, so her adopters will need to be prepared to continue her training and help her develop her lead manners so she can enjoy plenty of adventures. As she is a very large lady, it is important that her adopters have experience with her breed and understand her needs.

Candy has the confidence to be the only dog in the home, although she could potentially live with another large breed dog following a successful meet and greet. She loves to play and can be quite excitable, so she would not be suitable to live with smaller or more fragile dogs and she will need a home without cats.

Candy is an incredible girl, but she can be sensitive when she is worried or when she feels uncomfortable, for this reason, we feel she would be best suited to an adult-only home where her adopters can give her the time and space she needs to build trust and settle in.

She has arrived with a scab on the right side of her face that will be addressed during the time of her spay.

name: Nicole
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Nicole has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She was very scared when she first arrived and had clearly had little handling or socialisation, making human contact very worrying for her.

Nicole briefly moved into a foster home to learn about home life but returned to us following one incident where she became tangled in her lead and harness, panicked and nipped her fosterer. This was a single incident during a frightening experience, but adopters must understand that she can panic if she feels trapped or overwhelmed.

Nicole has now been back at the rescue for just over a month and is making lovely progress. She still doesn't like being picked up or handled, but is much better than she was and is increasingly comfortable spending time around people she trusts. She enjoys sitting in the play yard with her trusted people and responds brilliantly to treats, which are helping to build her confidence. She is a curious, cheeky little character who loves food, toys and snoozing in her bed, and she is even trying hard to be kennel clean.

Nicole loves other dogs and takes comfort from their presence, so she will need a kind and confident resident dog to help her feel secure and act as a role model.

She needs a calm, quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs. As she has never successfully experienced home life, she will need patience with house training and learning the basics of being a pet. Lead and harness training will also need to be introduced very carefully because of her previous experience.

Nicole still has a long way to go, but her curiosity and wonderful personality are beginning to shine through. With the right home, canine companion and plenty of time and understanding, we hope she will continue to blossom.

Our vets noted a slightly unusual heart rhythm, and a heart scan showed mild valve changes. She currently requires no treatment and is expected to live a normal, happy life, although routine heart checks and monitoring for future symptoms are recommended. She has been treated for a ear infection.

Nicole has been given the Gift of Life by Shirley Bourne

Nicole has been back at the rescue with me for just over a month now, and even though she is still a scared lady, I can definitely see she has made progress. She still doesn’t like to be picked up and handled, but she’s a lot better with it now than she was when she first arrived. She’s also more content just being in my presence now and will happily hang out with me in the play yard with confidence. I spend a lot of time sitting on the floor with her and dishing out treats every so often to stay in her good books. She does love her food, so this helps massively with building some trust with her!

Nicole does still have a long way to go until she’s anywhere near being a ‘normal’ dog, but she has a lot of curiosity in her and definitely some Shih Tzu attitude as well, so I’m hoping she will blossom in the right home. If you have lots of time and patience, and a space in your heart and home to welcome a special lady, please consider Nicole. I promise you won’t regret it!

Nicole is the type of dog that can instantly put a smile on your face, even when she’s not doing anything. She has such a comical and infectious energy, and I really just love spending time with her. She loves snoozing in bed in her kennel through the day and playing with toys too. She even tries her hardest to be kennel clean!! She’s very easy to look after day to day. So please… give her a chance.

Nicole has been in foster for a week and is a sweetie. She has a wonderfully inquisitive nature and loves investigating everything around her, which makes us chuckle! She is still very nervous about being handled and will bark when she's feeling unsure, but she is already making progress. She now takes treats from us and absolutely loves her food. She is also mostly clean overnight.

Nicole has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She is a lovely little girl who is understandably feeling very scared and overwhelmed to find herself here. It’s clear she hasn’t had much handling or socialisation before, so human hands are quite worrying for her at the moment, but we will continue gently helping her learn that hands can be kind.

Nicole will be looking for a calm and quiet adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She would really benefit from adopters who have experience with nervous ex-breeding dogs and who understand the patience, time and reassurance she will need as she learns to trust.

She loves other dogs and takes great comfort from their presence, so Nicole will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her feel safe and secure.

As Nicole has never lived in a home before, she will need patient adopters who are ready to help her learn everything about home life from the very beginning. She will need to learn new skills like house training and will also need to learn all about walking on a lead and harness.

With time, kindness and plenty of TLC, Nicole will begin to grow in confidence and let her personality shine.

Our vets have noted that Nicole has a slightly unusual heart rhythm, so she underwent a heart scan at our vets which showed some mild valve changes. At this stage she does not require any treatment and is expected to live a normal, happy life, although we would recommend routine heart checks and monitoring for any future symptoms.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. name: Gail
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I would like a home with one kind resident dog. I cannot live with cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I can walk well on a lead and harness, and am doing well with those I trust.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Gail has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived, she was a very scared girl who found human interaction extremely overwhelming and would often hide away. Since then, she has made some really encouraging progress and is gradually learning to feel safe in her surroundings. She is still a cautious girl who enjoys having people nearby but prefers to have her own space rather than seeking lots of physical affection. She will allow gentle handling and is slowly learning to trust those around her.

Gail will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle at her own pace. Gail is a sensitive little girl who can struggle with change, so she may take a step backwards initially when moving into a new home and will need plenty of patience and understanding.

Gail relies on other dogs for comfort and reassurance and will be looking for a home with one kind, confident resident dog to be her friend. She is still learning how to share her space and can be a little sassy if other dogs get too close, so she would be happiest with a calm dog who understands her boundaries. Once she bonds with another dog, she really enjoys their company and takes confidence from having them around.

Gail has started going out for walks beyond the garden and is making progress on her lead in quiet areas, particularly when somewhere familiar. She is not yet ready for busier roads and will need her adopters to continue building her confidence gradually. Her housetraining is coming along well, with very few accidents, although she will still need time to adjust to the routines of a new home.

Shortly after Gail's arrival, she started showing signs of back pain, as well as some weakness and unsteadiness. As she is a Dachshund, she had x-rays to investigate possible spinal issues. These showed several mineralised discs in her spine but no obvious spinal cord compression. She was given pain relief and crate rest, and initially returned to activity with the help of a supportive back brace. Gail has made a good recovery and is currently doing well. She is also receiving red light therapy and Bowen therapy, wears a therapeutic magnetic collar and has continuous access to warmth to help keep her comfortable.

Gail's adopters will need to be aware that any future issues relating to her back would be classed as a pre-existing condition and would not be covered by insurance.

Gail is a truly special little girl who has come such a long way since arriving with us. She is still very much a work in progress, but with a quiet home, lots of patience and the reassurance of a kind canine companion, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence and discover just how wonderful life can be.

Gail has been given the Gift of Life by Candice Sullivan

Gail has been making progress in foster and is gradually becoming more comfortable and starting to feel safe around the resident dogs. She is still a cautious girl who enjoys having people nearby but generally prefers to have her own space rather than seeking lots of physical affection. She is settled in the home, sleeps well and is happy to relax in her surroundings.

Gail gets on with other dogs but is still learning how to share her space and will let them know when she needs a little room. She is happiest around calm, respectful dogs who understand her boundaries.

She is becoming more confident with handling and will tolerate having her harness put on with a little patience and reassurance. She has also started going out for walks beyond the garden and is making progress in quiet areas, although she is not yet ready for busier roads. Her housetraining is coming along well, with very few accidents.

Gail is still very much a work in progress and will need a quiet, adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand her needs and can give her the time and space to continue building her confidence. She has been receiving red light therapy and Bowen therapy, wears a therapeutic magnetic collar and has constant access to warmth to help keep her comfortable.

She is making progress at her own pace, and we hope that with the right home and continued support, she will continue to blossom.

What incredible progress this girl is making! I'm constantly impressed and surprised by her.I only work with Gail 1-2 times a month, and I'm always blown away by how far she's come when I see her again. Some things that may not seem like much can be huge milestones for our ex-breeding dogs - three months ago, Gail could only be touched by a few members of staff and was very anxious in human presence; six weeks ago, she would only tolerate having her harness put on and being walked by the two people she knew best; two weeks ago, she was walking with a few people but still spending most of her time in the back of her kennel hiding, and would try to hide in corners if she saw anyone unfamiliar; and today, she went on a 20 minute walk with me, then cuddled in my lap afterwards! She even goes for walks with volunteers she's never met before and is incredibly brave meeting new people. When visitors walk past, Gail runs to the front of her kennel with her tail wagging.Gail is a lovely little dog with so much personality. She's going to be the queen of wherever she ends up, and she deserves to be spoiled rotten! Hopefully, Gail's perfect home is right around the corner. Until then, we'll keep on showing her all the love and kindness we can.

We're super pleased with Gail's progress over the last few weeks.

Initially, we started yarding her with other dogs. She coped really well but would tell them off if they were too lively and in her face. We then started kenneling her with a female Cavalier, and she coped very well and seemed happier in herself. We then added a lively Poodle, but Gail told her off, so now she's just with the Cavalier. So, we've learnt that Gail can cope day and night with a calm dog, and on night duty, I saw them snuggled up in the same bed.Gail's walking is much better, but only with the staff who know her well. She follows her nose on a walk and likes walking in longer grass. Gail will roll over for a tummy rub but is still a little unsure about too much fuss.Gail is a happy little girl, full of character, who loves to carry her favourite toys around, and she's not possessive of them.

Gail has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a very scared little girl who found herself extremely overwhelmed when she first arrived, and it was clear she was not used to much handling or human interaction. At the beginning, Gail was very wary of people and would do her best to avoid being handled, often using warning signals to ask for space. If she felt pushed beyond her comfort zone, she could panic and make poor decisions through fear. With time, patience and consistency from the staff she knows and trusts, Gail is making lovely progress and is beginning to show her softer side.

Although still a nervous girl, Gail is progressing well with the staff she has built relationships with and now enjoys attention from the people she knows well. She absolutely loves a tummy rub and has started to seek out familiar staff members for reassurance, showing that, given time, she is capable of forming strong bonds with the people she trusts.

Gail spent some time recovering from a back injury, but she is now showing no signs of pain and is back to her normal self. She happily trots around as though nothing was ever wrong and has recovered brilliantly. During her recovery she spent time on her own and, although she was later reintroduced to a previous canine friend, it became clear that Gail no longer enjoys the company of other dogs and does not like for them to invade her space. For this reason, she will need to be the only dog in her forever home.

Gail will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and understand the importance of patience, time and reading her body language. She will need kind, understanding adopters who will allow her to take everything at a pace she feels comfortable with and continue building her confidence without putting her under pressure.

She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her. She will need to learn all about home life, including house training and settling into a daily routine. Gail has also recently started her lead training and has surprised everyone with how quickly she has progressed. After taking just a few tentative steps on her first outing, she was happily trotting around, sniffing her surroundings and even confidently walking over to one of her favourite people the very next day. She is proving that, with gentle encouragement, she is capable of making wonderful progress.

As Gail has had previous back issues, we have used a supportive back brace harness to help protect her while she builds her confidence on walks. This is something her adopters may wish to continue using in the future for extra support.

Gail is a very special little girl who still has plenty to learn, but she has already shown just how far she can come with the right people by her side. She is looking for experienced adopters who are willing to invest the time and patience she needs, and in return they will gain a wonderfully rewarding companion as they watch her confidence continue to grow.

name: Tummy
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teenagers, aged 13+ who respect my space.

I will need to be the only dog in the home so all of the attention is on me!

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have previously lived in a home, so I may already know the basics!

I am on a special diet for bladder stones, please read below for more information!

11-10-26 Tummy is a lovely lady who originally came to us from a breeder and was later adopted into a home. Sadly, she has returned to our care after around 5 months as she wasn't getting along with the resident dog, so she is now looking for a home where she can be the only dog and have all of her family's attention to herself. She also cannot live with cats or small furries.

Tummy is a sweet and outgoing girl with a big personality! She loves toys and having a good play, but she also enjoys a quiet fuss and relaxing alongside her people. She has lived in a home before, so she may already know some of the basics such as house training, although she may need a few gentle reminders as she settles back into home life.

Tummy would do best with a family who has experience with Dachshunds and understands their wonderful but sometimes strong personalities, although she could also live with a sensible family who are willing to learn and understand her needs. She can live with dog-savvy teenagers aged 13+ who are sensible and will give her the time and space she needs to settle into her new home.

Tummy has never been left home alone before and so this is something her adopters will need to build up gradually with her to ensure she doesn't develop separation anxiety.

Tummy is an amazing little lady who has already had a change of home and is now ready to find her forever family. We hope that the right home will give her the love, attention and stability she deserves.

Tummy has previously been treated for ear infections and also has some hair loss that seemed to begin to grow back when she was in her previous home. She has a history of bladder stones and is currently on a specific diet to help with this, and this will need to be continued in the home. This will need to be monitored by her new vets and her adopters will need to be aware that should she require any treatment or potential surgery in the future it would not be covered by insurance.

Hungry has been given the Gift of Life by Jacqueline Wanstall

name: Max
description:
I need an active, breed experienced home that loves playtime!

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden to let off steam.

I walk on the lead but I can pull when excited.

I am house trained but I need to learn some manners.

I have been neutered and am ready for my forever home!

Max is a superstar Lurcher who has been returned to us from his adoptive family. They made the heartbreaking decision to bring him back as he was becoming dominant over the other dog in the home.

He is a very excitable, happy boy - essentially an overgrown puppy in a big body. Max is full of fun and enthusiasm and will need an active home that can meet his exercise and stimulation needs. He already knows some basic commands such as “sit”, “paw”, “lay down”, and “wait”, and he is eager to interact with his people. He is very food oriented, which makes training enjoyable and rewarding, and he already shows lovely food manners, waiting patiently when asked.

Max absolutely loves other dogs and gets incredibly excited when he sees a potential new friend. However, he is still young, full of energy, and not always aware of his size and strength. This can sometimes lead to him becoming overexcited, a little mouthy, and unintentionally overwhelming other dogs. He has been working hard on his social skills and has been socialising while wearing a muzzle for safe and positive interactions. This is purely as a precaution, and his future adopters will need to continue this training and take a responsible approach when introducing him to other dogs.

As he was too much for a more timid dog in his previous home, we feel that Max would be best suited to being homed as an only dog, provided he has plenty of appropriate socialisation with dogs of a similar size and play style. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Max has previously lived in a home, he is familiar with household sights and sounds and is house trained. However, he is still working on his lead manners and can pull when he gets excited. Ongoing training, structure, and consistency will be important, along with plenty of mental stimulation to keep his busy mind engaged. He would thrive in a home that can offer activities such as training games or even dog sports.

Max could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who understand that he can be a bit of a bull in a china shop. Any young people in the home will need to be confident and not worried by an enthusiastic dog who may jump up while he continues to work on his manners.

Max does struggle with separation anxiety and can become destructive if left alone for long periods, so he will need a home where someone is around most of the time and who is committed to helping him gradually build confidence with being left.

Max's new home will need a large, secure garden with 6ft boundaries, where he can let off some steam.

Max will make an amazing addition to a home with experience of similar breeds. He truly is a lovely boy, bouncy, affectionate, and full of life, with so much potential. He is a big-hearted lad who gives his whole heart, and with the right guidance, he will grow into an incredible companion.

Max has recently been castrated, and while he was feeling (understandably) sorry for himself for a few days after, he was brilliant going into the vets and during his recovery. Although he has had to wear a buster collar just to stop him licking at the area, he doesn't let that bother him and is such a good boy when you take it off to take him out for a walk and pop it back on when he's back in his kennel and he has been so easy to give his pain relief medication to as well, he really has been a model patient. He is such an easy dog to handle, given his size he is no issue at all.

During his recovery period, Max has only been on short walks so that he doesn't overdo it in the play yards, but slowly this past week he has been spending some time in our agility yard to have a run and you can definitely see that he is back to his full, playful self, running around, chasing a tennis ball and being inquisitive about anything and everything.

Max is a fantastic boy, and any time I spend with him is just so enjoyable and full of love and fun, he is such a special dog, I'm constantly scratching my head wondering why and how he's still here.

Where do I start with the wonderful ball of energy that is Max.

First and foremost, the question I ask myself and almost everyone that meets Max asks too, how on earth is he still waiting?! A young, handsome, intelligent dog who is BARRELS of fun. There’s something about Max that is just so loveable and he truly does capture people’s hearts. Many of the volunteers who walk him are always so happy to see him and enjoy their time together.

Recently we’ve been working on nailing a ‘touch’ command. When Max is focused he is such a rewarding dog to train. Sometimes his desire to please takes over and he waves his paw at me until I have to accept it (and of course reward because he's the goodest boy no matter what). He is also learning to be calmer when greeting people and has even had some gentle fuss from some children too. It remains true that Max cannot be homed with children under the age of 16, but it is so important for Max to have positive interactions with respectful children to prevent any reactivity / fear from developing. It also helps teach him to be calm when meeting new people, especially when they’re smaller than him!

Max brings such a unique type of energy to the rescue, he is such a joyful boy and truly comes alive when he is with his people. I threw Max a 1st birthday party and all of his favourite people came throughout the day to play with him and bring him yummy treats, fuss and cuddles. He had the best day and it was so touching to see how loved he is despite not being in a home.

We are doing our very best to raise Max into a well rounded, well socialised and well adjusted adult dog. However, he is at such a crucial stage in his development and has already spent 5 months in kennels. It’s no place for a young dog to grow up. Nearly half of his life spent in kennels patiently waiting for his second chance to come and take him home.

Despite his size Max really is just a baby and definitely a lap dog too. So if you have a spot on the sofa you can share, Max will happily join you and be the bestest friend anyone could wish for.

Myself and Max have formed a very close bond over the last few months we’ve been working together. We take daily walks, go to the big play yard and have plenty of cuddles and fusses.I’m not sure what it is about Max that keeps getting him overlooked, it could be his size or that he is like a big playful puppy or something else, whatever it is, anyone would be lucky to have this handsome chap in their lives, he will always put a smile on your face and he has such a good sense of humour, watching him having zoomies in his kennel yard while he’s jumping off the obstacles in there then stoping then going back round again is nothing short of entertaining, or when he’s fishing treats out of the paddling pool while simultaneously blowing bubbles with his nose.Max truly deserves the world, he is such a sweet and caring boy with a big personality and so much love to give, as well as his big size there is also a big heart and all he wants is to be able to fully give it to someone and finally find his forever home.

Max is a big, happy baby with bags of energy and so much love to give. He is an excitable, affectionate boy who adores attention and loves having people around him. He is always happy to greet you and be part of whatever is going on.

As Max is still young and growing, he is slowly learning his manners and how to greet people politely without jumping. . He will need adopters who can match his energy, continue his training, and give him the stimulation, guidance, and love he needs to thrive.

Max is a gentle, overlooked soul who is learning new things every day at the rescue, but he is missing the comforts of home. He cannot wait to find a family who understands him and can help him blossom into the wonderful companion he is meant to be.With the right home, patience, and plenty of love, Max will make a loyal and joyful best friend.

Since coming back into our care, Max has been working hard on learning how to socialise with other dogs. He absolutely adores them and gets incredibly excited when he sees a potential new friend! Because he’s still young, full of beans, and a bit unaware of his own size, he can sometimes be a little too enthusiastic. This can lead to him becoming overexcited, a bit mouthy, and unintentionally overwhelming other dogs.

To help him learn safe and positive interactions, Max has been socialising while wearing a muzzle. This is purely for his safety and that of other dogs, and his future adopters will need to continue this training and take a responsible approach when introducing him to new canine companions. Aside from that, Max is everything you’d want in a young pup he's bouncy, happy, affectionate, and full of life.

He’s very food oriented, which makes training a dream! He already knows commands like “sit” and has learned great food manners where be waits patiently until he’s told he can eat. Max thrives on mental stimulation and ongoing training, and with the right guidance, he has all the potential to grow into an incredible dog. Max does struggle with separation anxiety and can become destructive if left alone for long periods. He really craves human company so he’ll need a home where someone is around most of the time and is committed to helping him build confidence being alone gradually. He’s such a loving, handsome boy who gives his whole heart, and it would be wonderful to see him back in a home environment where he can truly thrive. As a young pup, he’s missed out on some important early experiences, so a patient, committed family will make all the difference in helping him become the best version of himself.

He is a very excitable, happy boy - essentially an overgrown puppy in a big body. Max is full of fun and enthusiasm and will need an active home that can meet his exercise and stimulation needs. He already knows some basic commands such as “sit”, “paw”, “lay down”, and “wait”, and he is eager to interact with his people.

Max loves other dogs but is often unaware of his size and strength, having grown into such a big lad very quickly. As he is still just a puppy, he is still learning about manners and can be mouthy and plays in a very typical Lurcher way. In his previous home, there was an incident when he was around 3 months old, where he was a little too rough and resulted in a small dog needing veterinary treatment. He has started muzzle training for off-lead play as a precaution, and he will need a home that understands Lurcher play styles and is confident managing this appropriately. We have been socialising him with dogs of all sizes on walks and he is doing very well.

As Max has previously lived in a home, he is familiar with household sights and sounds and is house trained. However, he is still working on his lead manners and can pull when he gets excited. Ongoing training and consistency will be important.

Max will make an amazing addition to a home with experience of similar breeds. He truly is a lovely boy. He is a big-hearted, affectionate lad who is still convinced he can curl up and fit on your lap.
